signals.topic: GCS storage.Client() created per-request causes connection pool exhaustion and cascading production failures
signals.summary: GoogleCloudEventServiceInjector creates a new GCS Client per HTTP request, exhausting connection pools under load. This directly contributed to a full cascading failure during the 2026-05-01 production incident.
signals.review_reason: Explicitly tied to a real production incident (2026-05-01) that caused cascading failures across the entire OpenHands deployment. While count=1, the review_reason provides explicit strong evidence of user-facing production impact. The bug is architecturally trivial (missing singleton reuse) but causes resource exhaustion affecting all SaaS users. P0 is warranted given the documented production incident.

source_issues.title: GCS storage.Client() created per-request causes connection pool exhaustion under load
source_issues.evidence: GoogleCloudEventServiceInjector.inject() creates a new google.cloud.storage.Client() on every HTTP request. Under production load this causes 'Connection pool is full, discarding connection: storage.googleapis.com' warnings. During the 2026-05-01 incident, this combined with runtime API timeouts and DB connection pool exhaustion to cause a full cascading failure. All 7 pods in the openhands deployment are affected.

signals.topic: RecallAction creates consecutive USER turns, causing HTTP 400 on Mistral/SGLang strict-alternation backends and stalling the agent loop
signals.summary: AgentController emits a RecallAction with EventSource.USER after every user message, producing consecutive 'user' role turns in the LLM request. Mistral-family backends enforcing strict role alternation reject these with a 400 error, causing the agent loop to stall on the very first prompt of every session.
signals.review_reason: This bug completely stalls the agent loop on every Mistral-family model served by SGLang or any strict-alternation backend — the agent cannot produce any output from the first user prompt onward. This is a main-flow runtime failure. While count=1, the described impact (complete session stall on every first prompt) represents a critical degradation for affected users. The workaround of disabling prompt extensions is undocumented and defeats a legitimate feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: RecallAction with EventSource.USER after a user message produces two consecutive USER turns, breaks Mistral / SGLang strict-alternation backends
source_issues.evidence: AgentController._handle_message_action dispatches RecallAction with EventSource.USER immediately after user message, creating two consecutive 'user' role turns. Any Mistral-family model served by SGLang, vLLM with Mistral chat-template, or strict-alternation backend returns HTTP 400 'Conversation roles must alternate user/assistant/user/assistant/...' and the agent loop stalls before producing any output. Reproduced on OpenHands 0.59.0 and 0.60.x. Workaround: enable_prompt_extensions=false disables the feature entirely.

signals.topic: Bitbucket provider authentication completely broken — deprecated App Passwords and missing API token support
signals.summary: OpenHands uses deprecated Bitbucket App Passwords for provider authentication, but Bitbucket has deprecated App Passwords in favor of API tokens. All authentication attempts fail with 401/302, blocking the core repo integration feature on both self-hosted and cloud deployments.
signals.review_reason: Explicitly blocks a core platform feature (Bitbucket repository integration) for all users on both self-hosted and cloud. Clear HTTP 401/302 error evidence in logs. While count=1, the scope (both deployment types) and the centrality of the blocked feature (repo integration is a primary use case) make this P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Bitbucket provider authentication broken (API tokens not working)
source_issues.evidence: Bitbucket App Passwords are deprecated. OpenHands still relies on old authentication format or lacks proper API token support. All attempted auth formats fail (username:api_token, email:api_token, x-token-auth:api_token). Affects both self-hosted and cloud versions. Error logs show '302 Redirect' to Bitbucket login page, then '401 Unauthorized'. This blocks a core use case: connecting Bitbucket repositories.

signals.topic: Switching agent_kind in settings UI causes 500 error due to stale fields leaking across discriminated union types
signals.summary: When a user switches between OpenHands and ACP agent types in the Settings UI, the Settings.update() method preserves stale fields from the old union member during deep-merge. Switching back to OpenHands causes model validation to fail with a 500 error because stale fields (e.g. agent_context: null) are invalid for the restored type.
signals.review_reason: The settings UI switching flow is a primary user interaction path. A 500 error on every round-trip between agent types means users cannot use both OpenHands and ACP agents in the same session, significantly degrading the multi-agent experience. Clear root cause identified in code. P1 is appropriate as it blocks a key feature path but does not prevent single-agent usage entirely.

source_issues.title: fix(settings): switching agent_kind leaks stale fields across discriminated union types
source_issues.evidence: Switching between OpenHands agent and ACP agent (Settings → Agent) throws 500 'Something went wrong storing settings' on the return trip (ACP → OpenHands). Root cause: Settings.update() deep-merges the current settings with the diff without clearing type-specific fields from the previous union member. OpenHandsAgentSettings fields like agent_context leak into ACPAgentSettings and vice versa. On switch-back, validate_agent_settings chokes on stale fields like agent_context: null.

signals.topic: Claude 4.x model alias-to-provider-ID mapping failure causing BlockUnknownError in Agent Builder blocks (AITextSummarizerBlock, AIListGeneratorBlock)
signals.summary: Following the v0.6.58 release, users who select Claude 4.x models (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.7) in the Agent Builder UI encounter BlockUnknownError — the backend fails to map the internal model alias to the correct provider ID, resulting in HTTP 400 'invalid model ID' errors from the Anthropic/OpenRouter proxy. Both AITextSummarizerBlock and AIListGeneratorBlock are affected, blocking the core summarization and list-generation workflows.
aliases: Claude 4.5 Haiku model ID error in AITextSummarizerBlock
Claude 4.5 Sonnet model ID error in AIListGeneratorBlock
Model ID mismatch for Claude 4.7 aliases in Agent Builder
signals.review_reason: Three distinct issues all rooted in the same backend model-alias-to-provider-ID mapping failure introduced in v0.6.58. Affected blocks (AITextSummarizerBlock, AIListGeneratorBlock) are core agent-building components. Users selecting Claude 4.x models in the Agent Builder experience immediate block-level failures with 400 HTTP errors — a clear main-flow block that prevents the summarization and list-generation use cases from executing at all. Multiple blocks affected, multiple model variants impacted (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.7), all still open. Count=3 meets P0 frequency threshold with direct blocking evidence.

source_issues.title: Model ID mismatch in AITextSummarizerBlock for Claude 4.7 aliases

signals.topic: ClawX bundled gateway unreachable on Windows (WebSocket handshake failure / memory leak)
signals.summary: ClawX embedded gateway fails to establish WebSocket connections on Windows 11, leaving the gateway permanently unreachable and preventing the app from functioning normally. Windows Event Log shows RADAR_PRE_LEAK_64 memory leak on ClawX.exe.
signals.review_reason: Core gateway connectivity failure on Windows that renders the entire ClawX app unusable. WebSocket handshake permanently fails, leaving the gateway in unreachable state. Accompanied by confirmed memory leak (RADAR_PRE_LEAK_64) in ClawX.exe. This is a main-flow blocking issue on Windows — the user cannot use ClawX at all. Single issue but strong evidence with detailed logs and environment specifics.

source_issues.title: Gateway not connected - WebSocket handshake fails (RADAR_PRE_LEAK_64)
source_issues.evidence: Gateway status unreachable (timeout) / ECONNREFUSED; WebSocket code 1006 (abnormal closure) or handshake-timeout 10s+; RADAR_PRE_LEAK_64 memory leak detected by Windows Event Log on ClawX.exe; port 18789 listens but doesn't respond to WebSocket; reproduced on v0.3.11 and v0.4.0-alpha.8 on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.22631

signals.topic: ClawX version manager fails to upgrade bundled OpenClaw to latest stable
signals.summary: ClawX controls OpenClaw versioning but cannot successfully upgrade the bundled OpenClaw to the latest stable release, leaving users on outdated versions and missing security patches.
aliases: ClawX fails to upgrade bundled OpenClaw
security patches not applied due to update failure
signals.review_reason: Version management is a core workflow — users cannot apply updates to the bundled OpenClaw instance. Explicit user complaint about being stuck on old version and missing security patches. This creates a sustained security risk as patches cannot be applied. Blocking issue for the update mechanism even though only one report is present, the impact is clear and unambiguous.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Openclaw version Update dont work
source_issues.evidence: User's OpenClaw shows v2024.4.11 but ClawX prompts update to v2026.4.26; clicking update button fails; OpenClaw CLI says it can't update because controlled by ClawX; user is stuck on outdated version and explicitly states they are missing latest fixes and security patches

signals.topic: Feishu/Lark plugin conflict: bundled feishu and legacy openclaw-lark both register same channel, causing duplicate messages and stuck chats
signals.summary: ClawX on macOS simultaneously loads both the bundled feishu plugin and a legacy openclaw-lark plugin, both registering the 'feishu' channel. This causes duplicate message handling (same message appears 3x), empty assistant messages, and stuck chat sessions.
signals.review_reason: Plugin conflict causes observable message duplication (same message appears 3x) and chat gets stuck. This is a clear workflow disruption for Feishu channel users. The duplicate channel registration is a packaging/migration bug introduced when ClawX started bundling the feishu plugin. Strong log evidence confirms the root cause.

source_issues.title: ClawX 0.3.8: legacy openclaw-lark and bundled feishu both register the feishu channel, causing duplicate message handling / stuck chats
source_issues.evidence: Both bundled feishu (id: feishu) and legacy openclaw-lark (id: openclaw-lark) register the same feishu channel; one incoming Feishu message recorded 3 times at 15-20s intervals; logs show 'channel already registered: feishu' and 'plugin tool name conflict (openclaw-lark): feishu_chat'; chat stuck with duplicate copies of same user message; macOS ClawX 0.3.8

signals.topic: QQ Bot delivery hint leaks into LLM reply body as [QQBot] to= prefix
signals.summary: QQ Bot extension embeds routing metadata '[QQBot] to=qqbot:c2c:...' as a system prompt prefix before sending to the LLM. Multiple models (DeepSeek, Qwen, quantized models) echo this marker verbatim in their reply, exposing internal routing metadata to end users.
aliases: internal routing metadata leaked to QQ bot users
signals.review_reason: Internal routing metadata ([QQBot] to=) leaks directly into user-facing bot replies. This is an observable data-leak UX bug — users see machine-generated internal routing strings in conversation. While not blocking, it visibly degrades the experience and exposes implementation details. Reproducible with multiple models. P2 because it only affects QQ Bot users and is non-blocking.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: QQ Bot replies carry leaked '[QQBot] to=qqbot:c2c:...' prefix when LLM echoes the delivery hint
source_issues.evidence: LLM reply body starts with '[QQBot] to=qqbot:c2c:2E18372D...' exposing internal routing metadata to users; confirmed reproducible with DeepSeek deepseek-chat/v4-flash, Qwen plus/turbo, and quantized models; user sees the marker as first line of bot reply

signals.topic: File write tool called but not executed on Windows — files not created
signals.summary: On Windows, the write/file creation tool is invoked by the AI but the actual file write operation does not execute. Users see tool call logs showing write was called, but the file is never created on disk.
aliases: Tool call logged but no file created Windows
signals.review_reason: Core tool execution failure — the write tool silently fails on Windows. The AI reports success but the file is never created, which is a critical workflow breakdown for users relying on file operations. User explicitly marks as reproducible and labels it as a bug.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 所有工具都没有被正常执行，显示调用了，但是没有执行
source_issues.evidence: User asks AI to create readme.md on D: drive with content; tool call shows write was called; write method is not actually executed; no file created; user confirmed no output; reproducible on latest release Windows

signals.topic: RealtimeAgent WebSocket 路径允许远程用户触发服务端 Python 代码执行（RCE 风险）
signals.summary: 当 RealtimeAgent 会话暴露 execute_python_code 工具时，远程 WebSocket 用户可通过提示词诱导 Agent 调用该工具，在服务侧执行任意 Python 代码，缺乏沙箱或审批边界。
aliases: remote code execution via WebSocket tool path
signals.review_reason: 该问题有明确可复现的用户影响证据（issue中提供了完整的复现步骤，验证了服务端文件写入），属于远程代码执行（RCE）风险，直接影响 AgentScope RealtimeAgent 的生产部署安全。虽然 count=1 不足 P0 阈值，但安全 RCE 风险属于高危，故标记为 P1。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:RealtimeAgent tool call path allows remote users to trigger server-side Python execution when execute_python_code is exposed
source_issues.evidence: 复现路径：WebSocket连接 -> RealtimeAgent._acting -> Toolkit.call_tool_function -> execute_python_code，无审批或沙箱边界。已验证可成功在服务端写入文件，确认 RCE。影响条件：RealtimeAgent WebSocket服务中暴露 execute_python_code 工具。

signals.topic: aget_last_run_output returns None when agent.id is auto-generated during arun()
signals.summary: When agent.arun() auto-generates agent.id from name, subsequent calls to aget_last_run_output() from a fresh agent instance (id=None) return None because the stored agent_id never matches entity.id.
aliases: last run output retrieval fails on fresh agent instance
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure — users cannot retrieve run outputs when using fresh agent instances, blocking HITL pause/continue workflows and session-based run history retrieval. Provides clear reproduction steps and minimal one-line fix.

source_issues.title: bug: aget_last_run_output returns None when agent.id is auto-generated during arun()
source_issues.evidence: When agent.arun() is called, agent.id is auto-generated from name. When a new agent instance (with id=None) queries the previous run via aget_last_run_output(), the stored agent_id does not match entity.id (None), causing the method to return None. This breaks the common pattern of creating a fresh agent instance to retrieve last run output, affecting HITL pause/continue flows and API calls that need to retrieve previous runs from session.

signals.topic: Anthropic context window errors not caught by CONTEXT_WINDOW_PATTERNS
signals.summary: Anthropic returns context window errors in format 'prompt is too long: X tokens > Y maximum' but CONTEXT_WINDOW_PATTERNS does not match this format, causing on_context_overflow handler to fail silently.
aliases: context overflow handler fails for Anthropic
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure — when Anthropic returns context window errors, the fallback mechanism does not trigger and unhandled exceptions propagate to users. Users expecting graceful degradation via on_context_overflow get errors instead.

source_issues.title: bug: Anthropic context window errors not detected by CONTEXT_WINDOW_PATTERNS
source_issues.evidence: Anthropic returns context window errors with format 'prompt is too long: X tokens > Y maximum' but CONTEXT_WINDOW_PATTERNS does not include patterns for this format. The on_context_overflow handler fails to trigger, causing errors to propagate unhandled. Users must implement manual substring matching as workaround.

signals.topic: Dependencies parameter unavailable when using agentos continue run
signals.summary: When using agentos continue_run(), run_context.dependencies is None, causing users to lose access to stored data like user_token that their workflow depends on.
aliases: run_context.dependencies is None on continue run
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking issue — when users continue a run in agentos, their dependencies (like user tokens) are lost, breaking workflows that depend on accessing user context during continued sessions.

source_issues.title: [Bug] agentos: continue run can't use dependencies parameter
source_issues.evidence: When using agentos continue_run(), run_context.dependencies is None. Users cannot access required data like user_token which they stored in dependencies. User asks 'How should I solve this problem, or can I only use Redis database to store user_token?' - indicating main flow failure for their workflow.

signals.topic: Google Drive allDrives search returns incomplete results without user notification
signals.summary: Google Drive's incompleteSearch flag is not exposed by search_files(), so users receive silently incomplete results with no indication of incompleteness, leading to missed files and incorrect conclusions.
aliases: Drive API incomplete results not indicated
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation — users performing Drive searches receive incomplete results without any indication of incompleteness, leading to potential missed files and incorrect conclusions. Data integrity issue affecting enterprise workflows.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Google Drive allDrives searches do not expose incompleteSearch
source_issues.evidence: Google Drive sets incompleteSearch=true when an allDrives query could not search every drive. The search_files() method does not request or return this flag, so callers receive silently incomplete results without knowing they are incomplete. Users may make decisions based on partial file listings.

signals.topic: AG-UI adapter receives CopilotKit context but does not pass it to Agent.arun()
signals.summary: CopilotKit frontend context registered via useCopilotReadable is visible in the /api/copilotkit payload but the AG-UI adapter never passes run_input.context to agent.arun(), breaking the entire CopilotKit context-sharing workflow.
aliases: CopilotKit context not passed to agent
signals.review_reason: P0 — key CopilotKit integration is completely broken. Frontend context is sent but the agent never receives it, making the entire CopilotKit useCopilotReadable workflow non-functional. Obvious experience degradation for any user trying to pass page state to their agent.

source_issues.title: [Bug] AG-UI adapter receives context but does not pass run_input.context to Agent.arun()
source_issues.evidence: CopilotKit frontend context (registered via useCopilotReadable) is visible in the CopilotKit Inspector and present in the /api/copilotkit payload, but the AG-UI adapter does not pass run_input.context to agent.arun(). The agent responds 'I can't see your page/content from here' despite context being sent. This breaks CopilotKit integration entirely.

signals.topic: OpenCode enters infinite loop after tool calls complete, blocking headless automation
signals.summary: After tool calls complete, OpenCode fails to detect the 'done' state and repeatedly calls the LLM with empty responses, causing the process to hang indefinitely at 0-2% CPU. This blocks all CLI automation and subagent orchestration use cases, wastes API quota, and has been a known issue since at least v1.1.65.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is completely blocked: the agent cannot complete any task that uses tools in headless/CLI mode without hanging forever. Evidence is strong with clear reproduction steps, log timelines, and multiple cross-referenced issues confirming the pattern is known and recurring across versions and providers. This is a primary automation blocker.

source_issues.title: Bug: OpenCode enters infinite loop after tool calls complete (Zen/big-pickle)
source_issues.evidence: Process hangs indefinitely at 0-2% CPU after tool calls complete; session loops on empty LLM calls every ~2.5s; blocks parent sessions that use opencode as subagent; wastes API calls/quota; must be killed manually (Ctrl+C or kill -9). Issue itself cross-references 5+ related open issues (#17516, #21250, #20096, #13841, #11865) all showing same pattern. Only workarounds are switching models/providers or manual kill.

signals.topic: Non-default FOSS models silently drop completions on OpenRouter integration
signals.summary: OpenCode's OpenRouter adapter silently discards completions for several non-default FOSS models (Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek-R1, llama-3.3-70b, GPT-OSS-120b). The same models work fine via direct OpenRouter API, confirming opencode's adapter layer is the culprit. This creates a hard ceiling for FOSS multi-agent orchestration.
aliases: silent completion failure OpenRouter FOSS models
Kimi K2.6 silent failure through opencode
signals.review_reason: Not P0 because count=1 but it is a significant user impact: the FOSS multi-agent use case is fundamentally broken as all non-default FOSS models silently fail. The issue provides strong comparative evidence (direct API works, opencode adapter doesn't) and clearly identifies the scope (multi-agent automation ceiling). Downstream users building FOSS orchestration stacks are blocked.

source_issues.title: Silent completion failure for non-default FOSS models on OpenRouter (Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek-R1, llama-3.3-70b)
source_issues.evidence: Spawned sessions reach 'idle' status with 0 assistant messages; prompts are sent but no response is persisted; logs show no error, just silence; same model + same prompt works cleanly via direct OpenRouter HTTP API, ruling out auth/network/model capability. The entire FOSS multi-agent orchestration stack becomes single-model (qwen30-only) due to this silent failure.

signals.topic: Kiro provider crashes with 'Y.languageModel is not a function' on every request
signals.summary: The native Kiro provider fails on every single request with a TypeError, making the entire provider unusable. The error occurs in the SDK call path and affects all Kiro models.
signals.review_reason: Complete and reproducible crash of a named provider on every request is a clear blocking issue, even with count=1. Confidence is high given full reproduction steps and error stack trace. Classified as P1 (not P0) because it is a single-provider issue rather than affecting core opencode functionality.

source_issues.title: Bug: kiro provider crashes with `Y.languageModel is not a function`
source_issues.evidence: Every request to the kiro provider crashes with TypeError; reproduced on both macOS and Windows; tested with 'opencode run --model kiro/claude-opus-4.5'; complete failure of provider functionality.

signals.topic: Agents get stuck during build commands (vite build, next build, etc.) requiring manual intervention
signals.summary: During common build commands (vite build, next build), the agent repeatedly hangs, forcing users to manually press ESC twice and resume the session to continue.
signals.review_reason: Build command workflow (a very common developer task) is frequently interrupted by agent hangs, requiring manual intervention. This is a recurring pattern ('it happens a lot') affecting a core developer workflow. Downgraded to P1 due to count=1 but represents a real recurring pain point in daily usage.

source_issues.title: Agents Get stuck when doing build commands
source_issues.evidence: Agent gets stuck for common build commands like vite build and next build; user must manually press ESC twice and resume session to continue; screenshot evidence provided showing the stuck state; issue is confirmed by multiple comments.

signals.topic: Token usage double-counted causing double compaction for Copilot Opus 4.7
signals.summary: OpenCode double-counts tokens when using Opus 4.7 through Copilot, causing token counts to jump from 100K to above 200K before triggering compaction twice in immediate succession. This wastes quota and may indicate incorrect token accounting.
signals.review_reason: Clear quota/cost impact: double compaction means the session gets compressed twice in a row, effectively discarding more context than necessary and wasting the user's quota. This is a billing/cost concern for paying users on the Copilot Opus model.

source_issues.title: Double compaction for Copilot Opus 4.7
source_issues.evidence: Token count jumps from ~100K to 200K+ then double compaction triggers immediately; specific to Opus 4.7 via Copilot; behavior not present a few days ago; indicates bug in token counting logic.

signals.topic: defaultHTTPClient panic from unsafe type assertion breaking OpenTelemetry transport wrapping
signals.summary: defaultHTTPClient() does an unchecked type assertion on http.DefaultTransport (*http.RoundTripper → *http.Transport), causing a panic when users wrap DefaultTransport with otelhttp for distributed tracing. The panic occurs during NewClient() construction even when WithHTTPClient option is provided (the panic happens before options are applied), making the SDK unusable for users following the standard OTel instrumentation pattern.
signals.review_reason: This is a P0-class panic that blocks the entire client construction path. It was introduced in v1.39.0 (2026-04-24) and persists in the latest release (v1.41.0). It breaks the standard OpenTelemetry distributed tracing pattern, which is widely recommended for observability. Users have no SDK-level workaround and must restructure their instrumentation approach. The panic is deterministic and reproducible on every invocation of NewClient() for any user who uses otelhttp.NewTransport().

source_issues.title: panic: defaultHTTPClient does unsafe type assertion on http.DefaultTransport (breaks otelhttp wrapping)
source_issues.evidence: Panic occurs during NewClient() construction: 'panic: interface conversion: http.RoundTripper is *otelhttp.Transport, not *http.Transport'. Introduced in v1.39.0, still present in v1.41.0 (latest). No SDK-level workaround exists; users must abandon global-otel-instrumentation pattern.

signals.topic: Build/compilation failure from invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 ordered-map type incompatibility
signals.summary: When a consuming module resolves invopop/jsonschema to v0.14.0 (due to Go MVS selecting the maximum version), the SDK fails to compile because schemautil.go uses wk8/go-ordered-map types while v0.14.0 switched to pb33f/ordered-map/v2. This is a transitive dependency conflict that blocks any project requiring the newer jsonschema version.
signals.review_reason: This is a real build failure that blocks projects from upgrading invopop/jsonschema. While a workaround exists (manual version pinning in go.mod), it is a friction that affects integration with other tools (e.g., code generators) that bring in the newer jsonschema version. This is a P1 rather than P0 because the failure is conditional on dependency graph composition and has a known workaround.

source_issues.title: Build failure: invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 incompatibility (pb33f vs wk8 ordered-map type mismatch in schemautil.go)
source_issues.evidence: Compilation error: 'cannot use orderedmap.New[...] (value of type *github.com/wk8/go-ordered-map/v2.OrderedMap) as *github.com/pb33f/ordered-map/v2.OrderedMap value in assignment' at schemautil.go:99. Go MVS selects the maximum version across all modules, so any project requiring invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 triggers the build failure. Workaround requires manually pinning invopop/jsonschema to v0.13.0 in the consuming module.

signals.topic: Embedded reflect.Type disables Go linker dead-code elimination, bloating binary size
signals.summary: The SDK embeds reflect.Type in internal/generated code, which forces the Go linker to include all types reachable from that reflection metadata. This disables dead-code elimination (DCE), causing unused SDK types and their transitive dependencies to be included in the final binary. The result is significantly larger binaries, especially impactful for CLI tools and lean container images.
aliases: dead code elimination disabled by SDK
signals.review_reason: This is a user-visible issue affecting binary size and build artifacts, confirmed by users whose dead-code elimination is disabled. While the impact is real (larger binaries, slower deploys for containerized apps), it is not a crash or blocking failure. It is P2 because the effect is non-blocking and a fix requires changes to the code generation pipeline (Stainless), not the SDK logic itself.

source_issues.title: bug: embedded reflect.Type breaks Go linker dead-code elimination
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states 'using this SDK disabled dead code elimination on our projects'. This is a confirmed behavior affecting any project consuming the SDK. Root cause is traced to embedded reflect.Type in Stainless-generated code. A cross-repo issue exists: openai/openai-go#609 indicates this is a shared Stainless SDK infrastructure problem.

signals.topic: Java quickstart文档缺失依赖配置导致示例无法运行
signals.summary: Java快速开始文档直接使用javac/java命令编译运行，但未说明如何配置classpath（Maven/Gradle依赖），且示例中声明的SDK版本2.20.0在Maven Central上不存在，导致用户按文档操作必然失败。

SDK version 2.20.0 not found on Maven Central

source_issues.title: Java quickstart docs: javac/java commands don't work without classpath setup, version 2.20.0 doesn't exist

signals.topic: Structured Output对Java字段始终标记为required，忽略@Nullable注解导致LLM幻觉值
signals.summary: 使用StructuredMessageCreateParams.outputConfig(Class)时，SDK的内部schema生成器将所有Java字段统一加入required数组，完全忽略@Nullable注解或Optional类型，导致Claude模型被强制生成假值（如字符串'null'、空字符串）以满足schema约束，而非返回真实null。
aliases: Structured output schema treats all Java fields as required
Java reflection schema generator ignores nullability markers
signals.review_reason: 功能级体验下降：用户使用结构化输出时SDK行为与Java语义期望不符，导致LLM输出数据质量劣化（产生非null假值而非真实null），且无用户端workaround。虽count=1，但用户提供了具体代码示例和schema证据，影响直接可测量。

source_issues.title: Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用@Nullable注解的字段被强制加入JSON Schema required数组，LLM被迫生成假值（'null'字符串、空字符串、'-'）以满足约束，即使system prompt明确要求留空。用户提供了可复现的代码示例和schema输出，并尝试过@JsonProperty(required=false)和Optional类型均无效。

signals.topic: VS Code extension fails to load on Windows UNC/network paths — blocking extension in corporate environments
signals.summary: Claude Code VS Code extension crashes with ENOENT when opening a workspace from a UNC network path. The extension attempts to resolve UNC paths as mapped drives and stores stale cached paths. All workarounds (clearing caches, reinstalling, simplifying config) fail. The extension is completely unusable for users working on corporate network shares.
aliases: VS Code extension network share crash
signals.review_reason: Extension completely fails to load on UNC network paths with no workaround. Affects corporate environments where users cannot map drives (non-admin). Clear user impact: main workflow blocked.

source_issues.title: Claude Code Extension fails to load on network paths (UNC paths)
source_issues.evidence: Extension crashes with ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat 'G:\Grupos' when opening folder from \\spwacd14\Grupos\... All workarounds fail (cache clear, reinstall, config simplification). Extension unusable on corporate UNC paths.

signals.topic: VS Code extension fails to install/activate on Windows — TypeError on file path construction

signals.review_reason: Extension fails to activate entirely on Windows with version 2.1.129. This is a regression that forces users to downgrade. Clear blocking impact.
