signals.topic: Bedrock streaming SSE error responses raise unhandled ValueError instead of proper API error type
signals.summary: When Bedrock SSE streams return error events (e.g., 400 with internalServerException), the SDK raises an unhandled internal ValueError instead of propagating a user-facing APIStatusError or retrying. This blocks reliable error handling in Bedrock-integrated production applications.
signals.review_reason: Bedrock users hit unhandled ValueError on production errors (HTTP 400 from Bedrock). SDK should propagate APIStatusError or retry internally. Clear runtime failure in streaming path.

source_issues.title: Bedrock streaming SSE events errors are not handled gracefully
source_issues.evidence: SDK raises unhandled ValueError('Bad response code, expected 200: ...') when Bedrock SSE returns error events. Stack trace shows crash in _stream_decoder.py. No retry, no user-facing APIStatusError. Affects production Bedrock workloads.

signals.topic: AsyncAnthropicVertex returns 404 for US/EU regional endpoints — async client completely broken in those regions
signals.summary: AsyncAnthropicVertex with region='us' or region='eu' sends requests to wrong endpoint host (e.g., us-aiplatform.googleapis.com instead of aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com), causing 100% failure rate for async calls in US and EU regions. Sync AnthropicVertex works fine with the same parameters.
aliases: Vertex AI async US region broken
signals.review_reason: Async vertex users in US/EU regions get 100% failure (404). This is a complete functional block for async workloads in affected regions. Sync works, confirming the bug is in the async path.

source_issues.title: Async methods NOT working with US/EU regions on Vertex AI - Gets 404 on endpoints
source_issues.evidence: AsyncAnthropicVertex with region='us' sends to https://us-aiplatform.googleapis.com (404) while sync AnthropicVertex correctly sends to https://aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com. Async client 100% broken in US/EU regions. Closed as fixed but remains a regression risk.

signals.topic: Claude Code Keychain prompt reappears after every MDM-managed update — generates enterprise helpdesk tickets
signals.summary: In enterprise MDM (Jamf Pro) environments without iCloud, the 'Claude Key' keychain prompt reappears after every MDM-managed update. Pre-creating the keychain entry via security CLI does not suppress the prompt. Users see this on every update cycle, generating unnecessary support tickets in regulated enterprise environments.
signals.review_reason: Enterprise MDM users see keychain prompt repeatedly after every managed update. Not user-blocking (Cancel works) but creates significant helpdesk burden at scale (100+ endpoints). Affects regulated enterprise deployments.

source_issues.title: [Enterprise/MDM][Jamf Pro] Keychain prompt 'Claude Key' appears after every update in managed environments without iCloud
source_issues.evidence: 102 managed macOS endpoints hit keychain prompt after every MDM update. Pre-creating keychain entry via 'security add-generic-password' does not suppress the prompt. Generates helpdesk tickets in ISO 27001 / NIS2 regulated environment.

signals.topic: Bedrock hosted Claude Opus 4.7 emits literal `<<<SENTINEL\n` prefix in tool input strings, corrupting all tool call data
signals.summary: When using claude-opus-4-7 on AWS Bedrock, every string value in tool input JSON is corrupted with a literal `<<<SENTINEL\n` prefix across multiple consecutive inferences. This corrupts the primary data payload of tool_use blocks, making the affected tools return unusable output.
aliases: Bedrock model corruption of tool input strings
SENTINEL token injection in Bedrock tool calls
signals.review_reason: A model regression that corrupts the primary data payload of tool_use calls. The `<<<SENTINEL\n` prefix is injected into every string value of tool input across multiple independent inference calls, making tool output unusable for any file-path→content mapping. While count=1, the evidence is exceptionally detailed (5+ reproductions, specific tool IDs, raw capture before parsing), demonstrating a reproducible systemic failure of the tool-use data plane on Bedrock.

source_issues.title: claude-opus-4-7 (Bedrock) prepends literal `<<<SENTINEL\n` to every string value in a tool's `input_json`
source_issues.evidence: All string values in tool input JSON begin with literal '<<<SENTINEL\n', corrupting file path→content mappings (globals.css, .tsx, .ts files). Reproduced across 5+ separate Bedrock inference calls in the same thread. Other tools in the same thread were clean — only this tool's string values affected. Raw Bedrock response captured before SDK parsing.

signals.topic: MCP server unreachability causes atomic request failure, blocking all tool use in multi-server deployments
signals.summary: When any one MCP server in `mcp_servers[]` is unreachable, the entire API request fails with HTTP 400. There is no `optional` flag, no per-server timeout, and the error message does not identify which server failed. This makes any production deployment using multiple MCP servers (filesystem bridge + search backend + domain tools) fragile, as transient outages on a single server take down the entire call path.
aliases: MCP server connection failure blocks entire request
one unreachable MCP server fails all tool calls
signals.review_reason: Production deployment blocker for the MCP feature: one transiently down MCP server atomically fails the entire tool-use workflow. The error message does not identify the failing server, making multi-server deployments non-diagnosable. The issue provides a comprehensive 4-challenger architecture review proving client-side workarounds are fundamentally insufficient, leaving users with no viable mitigation path.

source_issues.title: API: mcp_servers[].optional flag + structured error for graceful degradation on unreachable injected MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction with 2 MCP servers (fs + search) where fs is down. Request fails with 400 'Connection error while communicating with MCP server' — the healthy 'search' server is never reached. Works on claude-haiku-4-5, Sonnet 4.6, and Opus 4.7 across SDK versions 0.91.0 and 0.92.0. Cloudflare/ngrok tunnels flap legitimately in production. Client-side pre-flight probes are rejected by 4-provider architecture review due to SSRF, DNS rebinding, false negatives, and race conditions.

signals.topic: toolRunner drops defaultHeaders on follow-up requests, breaking Cloudflare AI Gateway and all header-based proxy authentication
signals.summary: The `toolRunner` helper does not forward `defaultHeaders` (and `baseURL`) on subsequent API calls within the tool-use loop. The first call is correct but follow-up calls (sending tool results back) lose all custom headers. This breaks Cloudflare AI Gateway unified billing (cf-aig-authorization), BYOK setups, and any proxy that authenticates via custom headers.
aliases: toolRunner loses custom headers on subsequent calls
proxy/gateway auth headers missing in tool-use loop
defaultHeaders not forwarded in toolRunner follow-up requests
signals.review_reason: Authenticated API calls silently drop required auth headers after the first turn in the tool-use loop, causing authentication errors that are hard to diagnose since the first call succeeds. This is a confirmed SDK bug (acknowledged by Cloudflare team) that breaks a major production integration (Cloudflare AI Gateway unified billing). Users must manually re-implement the entire tool-use loop as a workaround.

source_issues.title: `toolRunner` drops `defaultHeaders` on follow-up requests (breaks proxy/gateway setups)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed by Cloudflare team as SDK-side bug (linked cloudflare/ai#408). Reproduction: client with cf-aig-authorization header works for single messages.create but fails on toolRunner follow-up with 'authentication_error: x-api-key header is required'. Header is confirmed missing on the actual request reaching Anthropic's API. Workaround requires manual re-implementation of the tool-use loop. Also affects beta.messages.toolRunner.

signals.topic: Claude Opus 4.6 intermittently returns empty content array with output_config json_schema, breaking structured output feature
signals.summary: Claude Opus 4.6 frequently returns an empty `content` array when using `output_config` with `json_schema` format. The issue reproduces almost all the time. This breaks the structured output feature — the primary contract of the API. Workarounds (switching to Opus 4.5, enabling thinking mode, removing output_config) all degrade functionality or switch models.
aliases: Opus 4.6 structured output returns empty content
empty response from structured output on Opus 4.6
signals.review_reason: The structured output feature (a key API contract) fails intermittently on the latest Opus model, returning empty content with only 6 output tokens. This blocks the primary use case of output_config — reliable structured JSON responses. Users must either downgrade models, change model behavior, or abandon structured output entirely as workarounds.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.6 returns empty content with output_config json_schema
source_issues.evidence: Intermittent empty content array (output_tokens: 6) when using output_config json_schema on claude-opus-4-6. Reproduces almost all the time. All three workarounds involve degrading functionality: switching to Opus 4.5, enabling thinking mode (changes model behavior), or removing output_config entirely (loses structured output). Verified with full request/response payload including specific cache_control usage.

signals.topic: Subprocess stderr swallowed — SDK crashes during long-running sessions produce opaque generic Exception with hard-coded placeholder
signals.summary: When the bundled CLI subprocess exits non-zero during agent sessions (especially long-running ones with heavy MCP tool use), the actual subprocess stderr is swallowed and the original ProcessError (with structured exit_code and stderr fields) is destroyed. The user sees only a generic Exception with a hard-coded literal 'Check stderr output for details' — real exit code and real stderr are both inaccessible. This makes production failures completely undiagnosable.
aliases: Generic Exception with hard-coded stderr placeholder
ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+体验显著下降：长时运行Agent会话（非60+轮次时）一旦发生子进程非零退出，用户得到的信息是零诊断价值的占位符文本，根本无法定位失败原因。两条独立issue分别覆盖'长时会话崩溃'和'错误传播结构化信息丢失'两个子场景，根因相同（stderr未正确传递），均已在生产环境中复现。

source_issues.title: SDK subprocess crash during long-running queries with heavy MCP polling — stderr swallowed, error message uninformative
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced twice with identical stack trace at exactly 61 turns in unrelated agent sessions. Actual stderr from subprocess is swallowed; consumer sees only 'Exception: Command failed with exit code 1'. No diagnostic information available.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: ProcessError with structured exit_code and stderr fields is destroyed during propagation. stderr field becomes hard-coded literal 'Check stderr output for details' instead of real subprocess output. Users cannot catch ProcessError or access actual error data.

signals.topic: Async runtime context sharing failures — resource leaks, BaseExceptionGroup escaping, and cancel scope leaks block concurrent SDK reuse
signals.summary: ClaudeSDKClient is tied to the async context where connect() was called and cannot be safely reused across different asyncio event loop contexts. This compounds with two additional async cleanup bugs: (1) memory object stream resources associated with a query are leaked on completion; (2) SubprocessCLITransport's stderr task group leaks a cancel scope on normal query() completion, causing cross-task CancelledError that pins anyio's _deliver_cancellation in a 100% CPU loop. The result is that a second query() in the same event loop after a first one closes can crash the caller entirely.
aliases: anyio task group cancel scope cross-task exit
signals.review_reason: 影响明显：async cleanup缺陷在SDK并发复用场景下会导致调用方进程崩溃（BaseExceptionGroup escape）或进入100% CPU死循环（cancel scope leak）。三条独立issue均属生产环境并发使用时的高危缺陷，虽非高频但每个均严重阻断并发SDK使用这一核心场景。

source_issues.title: ClaudeSDKClient Cannot Be Shared Across Async Runtime Contexts
source_issues.evidence: ClaudeSDKClient instances spawn a persistent internal anyio task group tied to the async context from connect(). Cannot be safely accessed or reused from a different async runtime context. Breaks orchestrator patterns that reuse clients.

source_issues.title: BaseExceptionGroup escapes transport.close() on second query() in the same event loop
source_issues.evidence: On second query() in same asyncio event loop, transport's stderr task group surfaces BaseExceptionGroup[CancelledError] from __aexit__. suppress(Exception) does not catch BaseExceptionGroup. Exception escapes Query.close() and crashes the caller.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Identical anyio.create_task_group() + manual __aenter__/__aexit__ anti-pattern as previously fixed in query.py was not applied to SubprocessCLITransport. Normal query() completion triggers cross-task cancel scope exit, cancels caller's task, pins anyio _deliver_cancellation in 100% CPU loop.

source_issues.title: Resource Leak: anyio memory object stream associated with a query is leaked
source_issues.evidence: Query.close() cancels task group and closes transport but leaves memory object stream objects uncleaned. Confirmed leaked with PYTHONDEVMODE. Accumulated leaks degrade long-running process performance.

signals.topic: Bundled CLI hangs / times out silently in non-interactive environments (TTY detection failure blocking CI, Docker, cron)
signals.summary: The bundled `claude` binary hangs indefinitely when stdout is not a TTY, causing SDK queries to block forever in CI runners, Docker containers (without -t), cron/launchd jobs, and other headless orchestrators. Additionally, even when the binary is compatible, protocol-level initialization silently times out in container environments with no error signal to the caller.
aliases: TTY detection failure blocking headless environments
Bundled CLI silent timeout in Docker containers
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：SDK的query()调用在CI/CD、Docker、cron等非交互环境中永久挂起或静默超时，导致Agent工作流完全无法执行。两条独立issue均提供可复现的最小用例，affected use case覆盖orchestrators/CI runners/headless jobs等核心场景，属高频生产环境问题。

source_issues.title: Bundled `claude` binary hangs when stdout is not a TTY (pipe / file / launchd / cron / Docker)
source_issues.evidence: SDK hangs indefinitely on first query() call when stdout is pipe/file. Works correctly with TTY. Blocks all CI runners, Docker (no -t), cron, launchd, and orchestrator use cases.

source_issues.title: _bundled/claude v2.1.121 protocol-incompatible in container env (silent timeout on control_request:initialize)
source_issues.evidence: Inside Docker containers the bundled binary silently fails to respond to SDK's control_request:initialize message. SDK times out at 60s with no actionable error. anyio.open_process succeeds but no control_response is emitted.

signals.topic: fork_session() non-atomic write leaves orphan session transcript files on crash
signals.summary: fork_session() writes the new session transcript using a single os.write() call without a tmp+rename pattern. If the process crashes between os.open and os.close, a partial or empty .jsonl file is left in the project directory, corrupting session history and potentially causing downstream failures.
aliases: Orphan session transcript file on crash
signals.review_reason: 体验下降+数据损坏：虽然count=1，但fork_session()是Agent会话管理的核心操作，非原子写会在进程崩溃时留下损坏的session文件，可能导致后续list_sessions()等操作异常，影响Agent状态管理的可靠性。

source_issues.title: fork_session() write is non-atomic; crash mid-write leaves orphan transcript
source_issues.evidence: Verified in claude_agent_sdk/_internal/session_mutations.py, single os.write() without tmp+rename. Crash between os.open and os.close creates partial/empty <forked_session_id>.jsonl in project directory.

signals.topic: list_sessions() returns created_at=None when first JSONL record lacks timestamp field
signals.summary: list_sessions() returns created_at=None for sessions whose first JSONL record does not contain a timestamp field, even if later records in the same file do. This breaks session listing, sorting, and filtering that relies on created_at.
aliases: Timestamp field parsing from first JSONL record
signals.review_reason: 关键功能部分不可用：list_sessions()是会话管理的核心API，created_at=None会破坏按时间排序和筛选功能，影响需要按时间管理Agent会话的用户体验。count=1故降为P2。

source_issues.title: list_sessions() returns created_at=None when first JSONL record lacks a timestamp field
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: _parse_session_lite() uses raw substring search for 'timestamp':'' in first_line only. Later records with timestamps are not consulted. Breaks session sorting/filtering by creation time.

signals.topic: Bun --compile fails due to missing ./tempfile.js in published npm artifact (v0.2.96 regression)
signals.summary: Upgrading from v0.2.91 to v0.2.96 breaks Bun compiled builds because extractFromBunfs.js imports ./tempfile.js but that file is not present in the published package. npm correctly installs linux-arm64, but SDK runtime selects wrong musl variant on Debian glibc arm64.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct packaging bugs both introduced in SDK v0.2.x: (1) missing tempfile.js breaks Bun compiled builds, (2) musl/glibc misdetection on Debian arm64 causes runtime failure. Both block deployment in affected environments. Count=2 from separate but related regressions.

source_issues.title: Regression in 0.2.96: bun --compile fails due to missing ./tempfile.js import target
source_issues.evidence: extractFromBunfs.js imports ./tempfile.js that is missing from package contents and files list. bun build --compile fails with 'Could not resolve: ./tempfile.js'. Rolling back to 0.2.91 restores success.

source_issues.title: v0.2.119 picks linux-arm64-musl variant on Debian (glibc) arm64 even when only linux-arm64 is installed
source_issues.evidence: On node:22-slim (Debian 12, aarch64, GLIBC 2.36), SDK v0.2.119 requests missing musl binary despite only linux-arm64 being installed. Regression from v0.2.113 native-binary refactor. Last known good: v0.2.76.

signals.topic: EPIPE crash kills host process during subprocess startup-crash retry race
signals.summary: During a subprocess startup crash, the SDK's stdin write race condition causes an uncaught EPIPE exception that kills the entire host process, resulting in ~92s production downtime with all in-flight sessions lost.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed production P0: EPIPE bubbles directly to uncaughtException and kills the host process, causing real 92s downtime. Host applications running in persistent-session mode without defensive handlers are vulnerable. Root cause is an unguarded stdin write path during the subprocess exit race window.

source_issues.title: Uncaught EPIPE from subprocess stdin write callback during startup-crash → fresh-retry race (v0.2.120)
source_issues.evidence: Production incident: 92s full-gateway downtime, all in-flight sessions lost, mid-cron jobs orphaned. EPIPE arrives with no JS frame, exits process directly, kills host unless defensive handler installed.

signals.topic: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude instead of resolving plugin-loaded agent names
signals.summary: When Options.agent points to a plugin-loaded agent (e.g. 'my-plugin:test-agent'), the SDK silently ignores it and falls back to default Claude with no error, warning, or log line. The CLI's --agent flag handles the same name correctly.
aliases: plugin registry missing in SDK Options.agent
signals.review_reason: Clear user-impacting bug: plugin agent names silently fail in SDK but work in CLI. Users have no indication their agent selection was ignored, leading to incorrect behavior without any error signal. Workaround requires duplicating agent declarations via agents: inline block.

source_issues.title: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude for plugin-loaded agent names
source_issues.evidence: SDK resolves plugin agent names incorrectly: CLI returns 'I am TEST-AGENT-SMITH.' but SDK returns 'I'm Claude, an AI assistant…' (default). Silent fallback to default is worst failure mode — no error, no warning, no log line.

signals.topic: Slash command XML wrapper leaks through session resume, corrupting transcript history
signals.summary: The SDK wraps slash commands in internal XML (<command-name>, <command-message>, <command-args>) in the session JSONL transcript. On resume via query({resume}) or getSessionMessages(), this raw XML is returned as the user message text, rendering as garbage in chat UIs or being fed back into the model.
aliases: session transcript corrupted by command wrapper
signals.review_reason: Every SDK consumer that uses slash commands and supports session resume hits this. The wrapper is undocumented internal serialization that corrupts history display and can poison model prompts on resume. No error, just silently wrong data.

source_issues.title: Slash command XML wrapper persists in session transcript and leaks through resumed history
source_issues.evidence: On session resume, user message arrives as raw XML '<command-name>/context</command-name><command-message>context</command-message><command-args></command-args>' instead of original '/context'. Chat UIs display raw XML tags, and fork/append operations feed tag soup back to the model.

signals.topic: query() with minimal json_schema structured output crashes with null.effortLevel dereference
signals.summary: A minimal query() call with only outputFormat: {type: 'json_schema', schema: {...}} crashes internally with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel'). The internal effort-resolution path assumes UT2() returns an object but it returns null in a public SDK execution path.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed crash bug with a minimal reproducible test case. Makes structured-output usage unreliable in SDK environments. The error is a null dereference in an internal path, not a configuration validation error, indicating a latent bug rather than unsupported usage.

source_issues.title: query() with minimal `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema" }` can crash internally with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel')`
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic crash with minimal structured output repro (25 lines). Internal null dereference, not a user-facing contract error. Surface error is misleading unless caller inspects internal result.errors field. Affects SDK 0.1.75 and multiple older releases.

signals.topic: Native installer exits 0 but does not place claude binary, causing action to fail
signals.summary: The native installer reports 'Claude Code successfully installed!' while simultaneously emitting '⚠ claude command not found' warnings, then the action crashes with ENOENT when trying to invoke the missing binary. Affects plugin_marketplaces and general installation flows.
signals.review_reason: Two separate version regressions (v1.0.100 and v1.0.106) both cause the native installer to silently succeed while the binary is absent, crashing the action. This is a main flow blocker: the action cannot run at all when the binary is missing. #1290 is a fresh regression on the current v1 tag as of 2026-05-06, directly affecting any user with plugin_marketplaces enabled.

source_issues.title: plugin_marketplaces fails: claude install exits 0 but binary not placed at ~/.local/bin/claude
source_issues.evidence: Action failed with error: Failed to add marketplace '...': ENOENT, no such file or directory, posix_spawn '/home/runner/.local/bin/claude'. Installer exits 0 but binary not placed.

source_issues.title: Native installer reports '✔ successfully installed' while emitting '⚠ claude command not found' warnings (v1.0.106 regression)
source_issues.evidence: v1.0.106 reported success while emitting warnings; next step ENOENT'd trying to invoke the binary. Post-mortem — regressed in 106, reverted in 107.

signals.topic: Agent halts prematurely after Edit/Write phase with stop_reason: end_turn, never invoking Bash — multi-step workflows fail to complete
signals.summary: The agent reads and edits files but then stops with end_turn without invoking Bash, leaving multi-step tasks unfinished. Reproduced across seven consecutive runs.
signals.review_reason: Direct main flow blocker: the agent voluntarily stops before completing the core task (Bash invocations, git operations, PR creation). Reproduced seven times consecutively, rendering CI multi-step workflows completely non-functional. Strong user impact evidence despite count=1, as the review_reason documents the systematic, blocking nature of the failure.

source_issues.title: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with stop_reason: end_turn, never invokes Bash; multi-step prompts fail to complete (claude-sonnet-4-6)
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible across seven runs in ~14 hours. Previously-working multi-step prompt halted after edits with empty result string, never invoking Bash for verification, git ops, or gh pr create. Permission_denials: [] confirmed no permission block.

signals.topic: Action pushes commits when user only requested review/verification — workflow permissions: contents: read does not constrain it
signals.summary: The action makes and pushes commits even when the prompt only asks for review, and the workflow's contents:read permission does not prevent this because the action uses its GitHub App credentials rather than GITHUB_TOKEN.
signals.review_reason: Users experience unexpected content modification (unauthorized commits) when expecting read-only review. The workflow permission model provides false assurance — contents:read is silently bypassed. This violates the security model users rely on for CI read-only operations.

source_issues.title: claude-code-action pushes commits when only review was requested; workflow permissions: contents: read does not constrain it
source_issues.evidence: User requested only review and verification; action made and pushed a commit under claude[bot] identity. permissions: contents: read did not prevent this because the action uses GitHub App credentials, not the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN.

signals.topic: Action crashes with 404 Not Found when triggered by GitHub Copilot SWE agent — allowed_bots bypass ineffective
signals.summary: The checkHumanActor function calls GET /users/Copilot which returns 404 because Copilot is not a resolvable GitHub user. This crash occurs before allowed_bots logic is consulted, making allowed_bots: '*' useless for Copilot users.
signals.review_reason: Action completely crashes (not graceful failure) when triggered by GitHub Copilot SWE agent. The crash is deterministic and prevents any workflow using Copilot from working. Despite count=1, the crash is well-documented with clear root cause and affects a specific actor type.

source_issues.title: Action fails with 'Not Found' when triggered by GitHub Copilot (actor Copilot returns 404 from /users/ API)
source_issues.evidence: checkHumanActor crashes with 404 for GitHub Copilot actor. allowed_bots logic never reached. allowed_non_write_users bypass works for checkWritePermissions but separate GET /users/Copilot call in checkHumanActor still crashes.

signals.topic: validateHeaders fails for Max-plan OAuth tokens after subscription Pro→Max upgrade, blocking action initialization
signals.summary: After upgrading from Pro to Max subscription tier, the action consistently fails at SDK init with 'Could not resolve authentication credentials', despite the OAuth token being correctly passed and OIDC exchange succeeding.
signals.review_reason: Subscription tier upgrade (a routine, expected user action) breaks the action completely. Users upgrading to Max lose the ability to use the action, which is a critical experience failure. Root cause points to SDK validateHeaders not handling Max-tier tokens correctly.

source_issues.title: Intermittent validateHeaders failure with Max-plan OAuth tokens after Pro→Max upgrade
source_issues.evidence: After Pro→Max upgrade, action fails with Could not resolve authentication credentials. Token is passed correctly, OIDC exchange succeeds, GitHub App token obtained, but Claude Code subprocess fails at SDK init with both apiKey and authToken null.

signals.topic: False-positive filter silently disabled due to deprecated Haiku model causing 404 errors
signals.summary: The false-positive filter step calls the deprecated model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' which returns 404 on every run, causing FP filtering to be silently disabled. All raw findings are posted as PR comments without noise filtering, degrading review experience on every run.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point. The FP filter fails silently on every run due to a hardcoded deprecated model, resulting in all raw findings being posted as PR comments without any noise filtering. While the main scan still works, the downstream impact is significant: every PR with findings will be flooded with unfiltered noise, degrading the review experience on an ongoing, per-run basis. The failure is not a one-off error but a systematic silent degradation affecting every consumer of the action.

source_issues.title: False-positive filter fails with 404: model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' not found
source_issues.evidence: On every run the FP filter API call returns 404 for deprecated model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022'. Main scan completes successfully but filter silently fails — every raw finding is posted as a PR comment with no noise suppression, flooding PRs with unfiltered results.

signals.topic: Session hangs/freezes for extended periods with no progress signal and no reliable recovery action
signals.summary: Claude Code becomes unresponsive for minutes to hours during normal sessions at low context usage. Users have no signal whether the assistant is working, waiting, or stuck. Recovery requires sending another message or closing/restarting the client. Affects paid Max users who lose hours of session time with zero visibility.
signals.review_reason: Main session flow is blocked for extended periods with no user-visible signal. Clear user impact: paid users lose hours of session time. No reliable cancel/recover action exists. While count=1, the severity is high and the pattern is consistent across multiple independent sessions described by the user.

source_issues.title: Claude Code freezes for extended periods (often hours) during normal sessions at low context usage
source_issues.evidence: Session freezes for hours at low context (~25% capacity). No progress indicator, no error surface, no log. Only recovery is send another message or restart client. Affects Claude Max 20x subscriber losing hours of session time.

signals.topic: Background agent notifications not delivered — parent conversation stalls for minutes until user manually interrupts
signals.summary: Background agents with run_in_background:true complete work but parent conversation is never notified. <task-notification> either arrives with multi-minute delay or never arrives. Results in 5-10 minutes of dead time per incident. Users resort to running all agents in foreground as workaround.
signals.review_reason: Core background agent workflow is broken. Parent conversation stalls for minutes, indistinguishable from a stuck session. Clear time waste (5-10 min per incident). User had to implement workaround globally. This is a primary use case failure for multi-agent workflows.

source_issues.title: Background agent notifications not delivering reliably (macOS)
source_issues.evidence: Agent completes work, output file written to disk, but parent conversation receives no notification. Multi-minute delays or complete failure to notify. Pattern repeated across multiple launches. User added global CLAUDE.md rule to disable background agents. 5-10 minutes wasted per incident.

signals.topic: claude -p CLI billing routing error: rejected as 'out of extra usage' despite Max/Pro plan quota remaining
signals.summary: The claude -p CLI command is rejected with 'out of extra usage' even when the user's Max or Pro plan shows significant quota remaining. Requests are incorrectly routed to the extra-usage bucket instead of plan quota. Users may pay out of pocket unnecessarily. The tool is effectively unusable.
aliases: Max plan quota not applied to CLI
signals.review_reason: Primary CLI tool (claude -p) is completely unusable for Max plan users. Billing routing error causes false 'out of credits' rejection despite plan quota remaining. Clear cost loss potential (users topping up extra-usage pool out of pocket). Multiple historical reports confirm long-standing nature. High impact on developer tooling workflows.

source_issues.title: [BUG] claude -p rejected with 'out of extra usage' while Max plan 5h limit shows 35% remaining
source_issues.evidence: claude -p exits with 429 and 'out of extra usage' while Max plan shows 65% used / 35% remaining. Claude Desktop works fine on same account, same model. Multiple prior reports (#17263, #17694, #18446, #45203, #45095) with same symptom, all closed not_planned. User may pay out of pocket due to misleading error. Tool is unusable.

signals.topic: Bash permission prompt silently fails — tool rejected as 'user denied' with no dialog shown
signals.summary: When a Bash command falls outside the allowlist, the permission prompt does not display. After a 30-second timeout, the tool is rejected as 'user denied' — indistinguishable from a real denial. This is a regression of a previously-fixed issue. The harness fabricates a rejection on prompt-display failure, making it impossible for the model or user to know the true cause.
signals.review_reason: Critical auth flow regression. Tool is rejected without any UI feedback, indistinguishable from user choice. Causes failed tool execution and model confusion about whether to retry. The 30s silent delay is poor UX. Multiple open reports across platform/wrapper combinations confirm this is systemic, not isolated.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Bash tool rejected as 'user denied' with no permission prompt — regression of #9383
source_issues.evidence: Bash tool hits permission prompt path (command outside allowlist), no dialog shown, after 29.5s timeout tool_result returns 'User rejected tool use'. Confirmed: user did not click anything. Regression of #9383 (fixed Feb 2026). Same symptom reported open on macOS + Cowork, macOS + MCP, auto mode. Model has no signal to distinguish false rejection from real denial.

signals.topic: Git index.lock files left behind in worktrees during normal CLI operation, blocking all git commands
signals.summary: Claude Code CLI leaves stale .git/index.lock files in git worktrees during normal background git status polling. Lock files block git stash, commit, add, and other operations until manually removed. Recurs frequently within a single session, creating recurring interruption.
signals.review_reason: Regular workflow disruption for git worktree users. Blocks fundamental git operations (stash, commit) with no warning. Recurs frequently within a session. While count=1, related historical issues confirm this is a persistent pattern, not a one-off.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Stale .git/index.lock left behind in worktrees during normal CLI operation
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code leaves 0-byte stale lock files in .git/worktrees/<name>/ during normal operation. Blocks all git commands (stash, commit, add). Recurs frequently enough within a session to be a recurring interruption. User must manually remove lock files. Related reports on Windows and Desktop app confirm same pattern.

signals.topic: ralph-loop stop hook fails to detect promise tags due to transcript-flush race, causing premature iteration and manual cancellation
signals.summary: Two distinct bugs in ralph-loop stop detection: (1) The stop hook misses correctly-formatted <promise> tags emitted in the assistant's final text block of the same turn due to a transcript-flush race. (2) Unbounded mode (max_iterations: 0) has no safety net if the model never emits the configured <promise> tag, causing infinite loop requiring manual operator intervention.
aliases: ralph-loop infinite loop no safety net
signals.review_reason: P1: Two distinct failure modes in the same feature both lead to loop iteration failures — either premature (stop hook fires incorrectly) or indefinite (no safety backstop). The ralph-loop is a core workflow feature; these bugs force manual operator intervention and can waste significant compute/time on unbounded iterations. Count=2 from two confirmed, reproducible bug reports with different root causes.

source_issues.title: Stop hook misses <promise> tag emitted in the same turn — likely transcript-flush race
source_issues.evidence: Stop hook fails to detect correctly-formatted <promise>TESTS GREEN</promise> tag in the assistant's final text block across four consecutive /ralph-loop runs in the same project. Hook fires anyway, loop iterates, user must cancel manually each time. Reproducible and stable.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: add safety net for runaway when promise never emitted
source_issues.evidence: Unbounded /ralph-loop (max_iterations: 0) has no backstop if the model never emits the configured <promise> tag. Loop iterates indefinitely, only escape is operator intervention (rm/mv of .claude/ralph-loop.local.md). Distinct from prior session_id and promise-corruption bugs which are already fixed.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin silently wedges for multi-hour periods without errors, blocking inbound message delivery to Claude Code
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin's underlying grammY polling loop swallows network/timeout errors silently in an internal do-while, preventing them from reaching the plugin's outer retry logic. Process stays healthy, no errors logged, but updates never reach Claude Code for hours. Two field instances confirmed on the same day (2026-05-07) on separate production deployments (hermes-salah and hermes-nehal), both requiring restart-only recovery.
signals.review_reason: P0: High-impact main-flow block. The Telegram plugin is a primary integration channel; silent hours-long wedge with no error signal is a severe user experience failure. Confirmed by two independent production deployments on the same day with no self-recovery. No alternative workaround other than manual restart.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): cap grammy client.timeoutSeconds=90 to bound silent handlePollingError retries (multi-hour wedge)
source_issues.evidence: Silent multi-hour wedge: process tree healthy, MCP children running, getUpdates long-poll alive, but inbound updates never reach Claude Code. No errors logged. Two separate deployments (hermes-salah, hermes-nehal) wedged same day 2026-05-07 for ~34 hours. Restart-only recovery. Pending_update_count=0, getMe/getWebhookInfo clean. Root cause: grammY internal fetchUpdates do-while swallows and retries errors forever without surfacing to outer bot.start() rejection.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin self-exits mid-operation without triggering parent Claude Code respawn
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin's bun process exits cleanly during normal operation, removing bot.pid. The parent Claude Code does not detect this and fails to respawn the plugin. This breaks the server-side long-lived deployment model as the bot silently goes offline.
signals.review_reason: P1: Significant reliability issue for the Telegram plugin's primary use case (server-side 24/7 deployment). Plugin silently goes offline mid-operation with no respawn, requiring manual intervention. Distinct failure mode from the silent wedge (1766) — this is an explicit crash/exit, not a hang.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin (v0.0.6) self-exits mid-flight, parent claude does not re-spawn it (orphan watchdog tears down bot.pid)
source_issues.evidence: Plugin's bun process self-exits cleanly during normal operation, removing bot.pid. Parent Claude Code does not detect this exit and fails to respawn the plugin. Affects long-lived 24/7 server-side tmux deployment. Bot silently goes offline without user notification.

signals.topic: Context7 plugin silently fails to load MCP tools due to .mcp.json schema mismatch — plugin appears enabled but tools are never available
signals.summary: The Context7 plugin's bundled .mcp.json lacks the 'mcpServers' wrapper required by the schema used by all other plugins. Claude Code silently ignores the MCP server entry — the plugin appears enabled, skills load, but mcp__context7__* tools never appear in the session with no error or indication.
signals.review_reason: P1: Core MCP tool accessibility failure. The primary value of the Context7 plugin is its MCP tools. Users see the plugin as enabled with no indication that tools are unavailable. This is a complete functional failure for the plugin's core purpose, with zero user feedback about what went wrong.

source_issues.title: Context7 plugin's .mcp.json missing 'mcpServers' wrapper — silent load failure
source_issues.evidence: Plugin's .mcp.json has {context7: {...}} instead of {mcpServers: {context7: {...}}}. Claude Code silently ignores the entry — plugin appears enabled, skills load, but mcp__context7__* tools never appear. No error, no indication. All other plugins use the mcpServers wrapper schema.

signals.topic: fakechat MCP server orphan-holds its port after parent Claude Code exits abnormally, preventing subsequent sessions from starting
signals.summary: The fakechat channel server does not self-terminate when its parent Claude Code process dies abnormally (crash, kill -9, terminal close). The orphaned bun process is re-parented to init and continues holding the FAKECHAT_PORT (default 8787). Subsequent sessions fail to start because the port is already in use.
signals.review_reason: P1: Prevents subsequent fakechat sessions from starting. Users must manually identify and kill the orphaned process before restarting. Breaks the primary development workflow for users relying on fakechat as a local testing channel.

source_issues.title: fakechat MCP server can outlive Claude Code and orphan-hold its port
source_issues.evidence: fakechat channel server does not self-terminate on abnormal parent exit (crash, kill -9, terminal close without /exit, or any path that bypasses clean SIGTERM through MCP stdio pipe). Orphaned bun server keeps holding FAKECHAT_PORT. Next session started with --channels plugin:fakechat fails to bind port.

signals.topic: Plugin installer loads all skills instead of only those declared in marketplace.json, causing duplicate skills and token waste
signals.summary: The plugin install mechanism ignores the `skills` array in marketplace.json and instead loads every skill directory in the repo cache. When users install both document-skills and example-skills plugins, both load identical sets of 17 skills instead of their intended 4 each, wasting ~50k tokens and polluting the context window.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users confirm the plugin install mechanism ignores marketplace.json skill declarations, loading all 17 skills. This causes measurable token waste (~50k per session), context pollution, and defeats the purpose of the plugin/package distinction. This is a packaging/release defect that directly impacts Claude Code usage quality.

source_issues.title: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical content, causing duplicate skills
source_issues.evidence: User reports both plugins install all 17 skills instead of their intended subsets, causing ~50k wasted tokens and duplicate entries in /context. Reproduction steps provided with v2.0.76 on macOS.

source_issues.title: document-skills plugin loads all skills from repo instead of only declared ones in marketplace.json
source_issues.evidence: User reports installing document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills loads all 17 skills instead of the 4 declared in marketplace.json. Root cause identified: plugin loader loads all directories without filtering against the skills array.

signals.topic: npx skills add installs skills to wrong directory ~/.agents/skills/ while Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills
signals.summary: The `npx skills add` command installs skills to ~/.agents/skills/ but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills/, leaving users' manually installed skills invisible to Claude Code.
aliases: skills not found due to wrong path
signals.review_reason: Skills installed via npx end up in a directory Claude Code does not scan, making the entire skill installation workflow broken for affected users. The user explicitly asks 'Has this issue been resolved?' indicating a confirmed blocking issue. Primary workflow for manual skill installation is broken for this tool.

source_issues.title: npx skills add may install skills to ~/.agents/skills/, but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills
source_issues.evidence: User reports npx skills add installs to ~/.agents/skills/ but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills/. Skills added via npx are invisible to Claude Code. User asks if this has been resolved.

signals.topic: MCP returns excess uncompressed data causing context congestion when used with database-related MCPs
signals.summary: When using MCP with database-related tools via Claude Code, the MCP returns large amounts of uncompressed data that congests the context window, making database MCPs impractical for users with substantial datasets.
signals.review_reason: MCP returning large uncompressed data directly congests the context window, rendering database-related MCP integrations impractical. While only one report, the described behavior (context congestion from unconstrained data returns) is a clear functional degradation that blocks practical MCP usage with any non-trivial data source.

source_issues.title: MCP returns excess data
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states MCP returns data without compression and that large data returns from database-related MCPs cause 'congestion context'. Requests engineering optimization.

signals.topic: eval-viewer cannot find per-eval metadata because it checks two directory levels too deep
signals.summary: The skill-creator's eval-viewer tool fails to find eval_metadata.json at the location specified by SKILL.md instructions. aggregate_benchmark.py reads from the correct location but eval-viewer's generate_review.py checks two levels deeper, causing every evaluation run to show '(No prompt found)'.
signals.review_reason: eval-viewer fails to find metadata at the documented location, breaking the skill evaluation workflow. Every run shows '(No prompt found)', making the tool's primary output unreliable. This is a developer tooling defect that prevents proper evaluation of skills created with the skill-creator.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: eval-viewer doesn't find per-eval metadata
source_issues.evidence: User reports eval-viewer always renders '(No prompt found)' even though the metadata file exists at the correct location per SKILL.md. Confirmed path mismatch: eval-viewer checks run_dir/ and run_dir.parent/ but metadata sits at run_dir.parent.parent/. Full repro steps provided.

signals.topic: Queued message interjection silently deletes user input without adding to conversation
signals.summary: When a user types a message while Goose is processing (creating a queued card) and clicks Send to interject, the message is silently dropped — it stops the current task but the interjected message never appears in conversation history and Goose has no memory of it. Two separate issues confirm the same root cause.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the same interjection flow silently discards user input. This is a data-loss bug where the user's typed message simply disappears — no error, no record, no LLM call. It directly breaks the core interjection workflow and leaves Goose with no memory of the user's message.

source_issues.title: Queued message lost when clicking Send — message removed from queue but never added to conversation history
source_issues.evidence: User clicks Send on queued message: current task stops but message never appears in conversation history. User asks Goose to continue or reference the message — Goose has no knowledge of it. Silent data loss.

source_issues.title: Queued message interrupt kills processing and deletes the queued message
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible: clicking Send icon on queued card to interject stops processing AND deletes the queued message — it never gets delivered. User must retype. Confirmed on fresh macOS reinstall.

signals.topic: MCP elicitation response not delivered to server causing session to hang indefinitely
signals.summary: After a user responds to an MCP elicitation prompt in Goose Desktop, the response is not forwarded to the MCP server. The MCP server waits indefinitely and Goose Desktop also hangs, completely blocking the MCP tool workflow.
aliases: elicitation result not sent to MCP server
signals.review_reason: MCP elicitation is a critical workflow mechanism. When the response is not forwarded, both the MCP server and Goose Desktop hang indefinitely — a complete workflow block for any user relying on MCP tools with elicitation. Screen recordings and user logs provide direct evidence of the hang and lost response.

source_issues.title: Race condition while connecting to MCP servers & elicitation errors
source_issues.evidence: After users submit an elicitation response in Goose Desktop, the result is not successfully delivered to the MCP server, causing Goose Desktop to hang forever. LLM is no longer responsive after elicitation. Separate race condition where MCP servers are spawned three times. Screen recordings attached showing the hang.

signals.topic: Session silently hangs after chat-mode text-only response with no user indication
signals.summary: After an agentic session enters chat mode and the LLM returns a text-only response (no tool calls), the entire session stalls silently. Goose continues accepting and storing messages in the DB but makes zero LLM calls and generates no responses, leaving the user stuck for extended periods with no indication anything is wrong.
signals.review_reason: Main-flow session completely dead for 40+ minutes with zero indication to the user. This is a session-killing bug where Goose appears alive (accepting input, showing UI) but is permanently non-responsive. Database logs and request traces provide unambiguous evidence of the blockage.

source_issues.title: Session silently hangs after chat-mode response — subsequent user messages receive no response
source_issues.evidence: 40 minutes of complete silence confirmed via database logs and llmrouter metrics: zero requests to LLM, zero assistant messages written to DB. User sent multiple messages that were stored in DB but never received responses. No indication given to user that session was dead. Full database evidence attached.

signals.topic: CLI installer downloads wrong (glibc) binary on Alpine/musl Linux causing complete installation failure
signals.summary: On Alpine Linux, the official CLI installer downloads the glibc-targeted binary (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) instead of a musl build, causing immediate failures with missing symbol errors. The tool is completely unusable out of the box.
aliases: glibc symbols not found on Alpine
signals.review_reason: Complete tool failure on a specific but growing Linux distribution (Alpine). Installer selects the wrong binary class, making the tool entirely unusable from the first command. Multiple missing symbol errors confirm the binary is fundamentally incompatible. Despite count=1, the severity is maximum — zero functionality — and the fix is a clear build artifact gap.

source_issues.title: Installer downloads glibc Linux binary on Alpine/musl and fails with missing symbols
source_issues.evidence: Installer downloads goose-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.bz2 on Alpine/musl. Binary immediately fails during 'goose configure' with: fcntl64 symbol not found, __res_init not found, __vsnprintf_chk, __snprintf_chk, __memcpy_chk missing. Tool is completely unusable. No musl release artifact exists.

signals.topic: tmux UI displays extra spaces and footer overflow every minute during time refresh
signals.summary: When running Goose CLI inside tmux, the footer date/time refresh adds extra spaces and the footer overflows by one character every minute, creating a progressively degrading visual layout.
signals.review_reason: Reproducible visual degradation in tmux terminal. Not blocking (tool still functional) but creates poor CLI experience with accumulating visual clutter. Count=1 and single-environment scope warrant P2 priority.

source_issues.title: goose cli adding spaces and extra footer line in tmux
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: start tmux, run goose CLI, footer date/time refresh adds extra spaces every minute. Suspected cause: Goose icon taking 3 characters instead of expected 2. Screenshot attached showing overflow.

signals.topic: Storage state persistence broken in Stagehand v3 — userDataDir doesn't work, storageState() method missing, blocking authentication workflows
signals.summary: Stagehand v3 removed Playwright dependency and broke storage state persistence. The userDataDir option is ignored (Chrome directory never created), the storageState() method is missing from context objects, and authentication state cannot be persisted between sessions. Users migrating from v2 to v3 have no official way to maintain login sessions, forcing fragile manual cookie/localStorage extraction workarounds that fail on HttpOnly cookies.
aliases: userDataDir not working in Stagehand v3
authentication state not persisting between sessions
Stagehand v3 migration breaks auth persistence
no way to persist cookies and login state in v3
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user workflow blocking issue. The v3 architectural change (removing Playwright dependency) removed critical authentication persistence functionality without providing a replacement. Users cannot persist login sessions across test runs, forcing manual cookie extraction workarounds. The issue has 7 comments showing community impact. The 'no error thrown, directory never created' behavior means users cannot even detect the failure mode. Main workflow for automation testing (authenticated flows) is directly blocked.

source_issues.title: Storage state persistence broken in Stagehand v3 - userDataDir doesn't work, storageState() method missing
source_issues.evidence: userDataDir directory is never created; storageState() method not available on stagehand.context or page.context(); authentication state cannot be persisted between sessions; workaround misses HttpOnly cookies; 7 comments on the issue indicating community interest and impact

signals.topic: 配置文件不支持多环境隔离（test/stage/prod），生产部署风险高

signals.review_reason: 配置文件不支持多环境隔离，导致生产/staging/testing环境共用同一配置，tracing数据也无法区分。影响部署流程规范化和问题排查，属于生产部署改进项，归为P2。count=2来自两个相关issue合并。

source_issues.title: .env , config.yaml 等配置文件支持多环境隔离
source_issues.evidence: 用户请求在.env和config.yaml中支持通过$ENV变量区分test/stage/prod等不同环境，满足多环境隔离需求。

source_issues.title: add tag
source_issues.evidence: langfuse参数配置中缺少environment标签，多套环境tracing数据无法区分，难以排查问题（从#2755评论中衍生出的需求）。

signals.topic: event_store存储content仅支持dict类型，list类型导致SQLite插入失败（ProgrammingError）
signals.summary: 工具调用返回list类型content时，event_store的SQLite插入语句报错DataError/ProgrammingError，导致run_events数据完全无法持久化，属核心存储流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: 用户运行包含多个tool_calls的对话时，工具返回的content为list类型，event_store的SQLite写入因类型不匹配而抛出ProgrammingError，导致run_events持久化流程完全中断，数据丢失。属核心数据存储流程阻断，用户影响明确（sqlite3.ProgrammingError with Error binding parameter 6），有完整错误栈支撑。虽然count=1，但review_reason给出强用户影响证据（完整数据丢失 + 主流程阻断），满足P0豁免条件。

source_issues.title: [Bug] event_store存储content仅处理了dict的情况，但content存在为list的情况导致存储失败
source_issues.evidence: SQLite ProgrammingError: Error binding parameter 6: type 'list' is not supported。INSERT INTO run_events语句中content字段收到list类型数据（Command对象序列化后的列表），直接抛出ProgrammingError，导致run结束后batch存储完全失败，数据丢失。

signals.topic: 多工具调用响应缺失对应tool消息导致OpenAI 400 BadRequestError，会话冻结
signals.summary: 当LLM在单次响应中返回多个tool_calls时，框架未将所有tool响应正确追加回messages数组，导致后续API请求违反OpenAI兼容性规则，抛出400 BadRequestError并使会话冻结。
signals.review_reason: 当LLM返回多tool_calls时，框架序列化工具响应不完整，导致OpenAI API返回400 BadRequestError，middleware 3次重试全部失败，会话进入冻结状态无法继续。属agent主流程阻断，用户影响极其明确（有错误日志、截图、时间线），issue标签为critical。虽然count=1，但属于主流程阻断级别用户痛点，满足P0豁免条件。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Multi-tool_calls response missing corresponding tool messages (OpenAI 400 BadRequestError)
source_issues.evidence: openai.BadRequestError: An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'。middleware重试3次全部失败，session stuck/frozen，有完整日志时间线和截图证据。Issue标记为critical。

This is a critical, core feature failure that prevents users from getting code completions at all. The symptom of a silent, empty UI (even when server returns valid data) is particularly alarming as it provides no diagnostic information.

signals.topic: BrightData SERP tool generates malformed search URLs due to JavaScript template literal syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all Google/Bing/Yandex searches
signals.summary: BrightDataSearchTool uses ${query} (JS template literal) instead of {query} (Python f-string) in get_search_url(), producing URLs like https://www.google.com/search?q=$test instead of ?q=test. All three search engines are affected.
aliases: template literal syntax in Python f-string
signals.review_reason: A confirmed code-level bug in a core tool that makes the BrightDataSearchTool produce 100% broken search URLs for every user. The bug is deterministic and reproducible — every search query prepends a '$' character, making all BrightData SERP searches fail or return irrelevant results. This is a complete functional breakdown of a shipped feature with no user workaround.

source_issues.title: [BUG] BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed code-level bug in get_search_url() method: f'...${query}' produces literal '$test' instead of 'test'. Affects all three engines (Google, Bing, Yandex). Python interpreter verification included in issue body.

signals.topic: Async workflows using akickoff() with output_json or output_pydantic block the event loop via synchronous LLM.call() in converter module
signals.summary: When an async workflow (akickoff) uses Task(output_json=...) or Task(output_pydantic=...), the _export_output path calls synchronous self.llm.call() instead of await llm.acall(), blocking the event loop.
aliases: event loop blocking in async output conversion
sync LLM call in async flow
signals.review_reason: Users running async workflows (akickoff) with structured output requirements encounter event loop blocking, which can hang or crash the workflow. This directly breaks legitimate async usage patterns with output conversion features. While closed, it represents a real async/sync mixing bug that blocks async-first users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Do not invoke synchronous call() on LLM from asynchronous workflow in _export_output / converter
source_issues.evidence: In async workflow via akickoff() with Task(output_json=...) or Task(output_pydantic=...), _export_output delegates to converter module which calls synchronous self.llm.call(), blocking the event loop. Referenced from task.py lines 605, 1023, 1258.

signals.topic: result_as_answer=True causes agent to accept tool error output as final answer, bypassing agent reflection on tool failure
signals.summary: When a tool with result_as_answer=True fails, the agent ignores the failure and uses the error message as its final answer instead of reflecting on the failure. This removes the agent's ability to retry or handle tool errors gracefully.
aliases: agent accepts tool error as valid output
signals.review_reason: A tool with result_as_answer=True blindly accepts error output as a valid final answer, removing the agent's ability to reflect and recover from tool failures. The evidence shows explicit crew logs with error messages surfacing as final outputs, demonstrating a real broken trust chain in agentic workflows. Users relying on result_as_answer for tool integration have no way to distinguish success from failure.

source_issues.title: [BUG] If result_as_answer=true is set, then irrespective of tool's failure or success, tool output which essentially is error returned will become final answer of agent
source_issues.evidence: User provides log evidence showing 'Error executing tool: exceptions must derive from BaseException' becoming the final crew output. Agent ignores tool success/failure and makes tool output its own when result_as_answer=True.

signals.topic: Dual agent executor paths (CrewAgentExecutor vs AgentExecutor) cause silent behavioral divergence with no user-visible indication
signals.summary: Agent.kickoff() hard-codes experimental AgentExecutor while Agent.execute_task() uses CrewAgentExecutor by default. This causes the reasoning step to be silently skipped in one path, with 27 files referencing both classes and two separate test suites.
signals.review_reason: An architectural defect where two production executor classes are both in the hot path, causing silent behavioral divergence (reasoning step silently skipped in one path) with no user-visible indication. Since Agent.kickoff() hard-codes one executor and Agent.execute_task() defaults to the other, the same Agent instance produces different behavior depending on which method is called. This affects all multi-agent workflows and makes it impossible for users to predict which executor runs their agent logic.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Two parallel agent executors (CrewAgentExecutor vs experimental AgentExecutor) cover the same responsibility — pick a winner
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed architectural defect: Agent.kickoff() hard-codes AgentExecutor (line 1402 of agent/core.py) while Agent.execute_task() uses CrewAgentExecutor as default (lines 323-330). handle_reasoning() is gated off for AgentExecutor (line 515), causing silent behavioral divergence. 27 files reference both classes. Two separate test suites exist (2046 lines vs 454 lines).

signals.topic: HITL pre-review with learn=True silently falls back to raw output on any exception without logging or event emission
signals.summary: When @human_feedback(..., learn=True) is used and lessons are recalled, _pre_review_with_lessons catches all exceptions and returns raw output with no warning, log, or event. Users cannot distinguish pre-reviewed output from raw output.
signals.review_reason: Users who enable human_feedback with learn=True have pre-review safeguards silently bypassed on any exception (network, auth, LLM, structured-output). The system continues as if pre-review succeeded, and users have no signal that pre-review failed — creating a silent trust violation where users believe output was reviewed when it was not.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: HITL pre-review fails open and silently bypasses automated safeguards
source_issues.evidence: Code in lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/human_feedback.py: except Exception: return method_output. No exception propagation, no warning/error log, flow continues normally. Users cannot distinguish pre-reviewed output from raw model output.

signals.topic: CLI falls back to binary name as pattern, producing misleading 'pattern not found' error that blocks common invocations

This breaks the README yt() shell helper, fabric-ai update-style invocations, and any -y URL --transcript without a -p flag. Users misinterpret the error as "fabric not installed" or "Homebrew packaging broken".

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Misleading "pattern '<binary-name>' not found" when no pattern is specified, plus README zsh yt() example is broken since #1960

signals.topic: DeepSeek reasoning_content field dropped in message serialization, causing 400 errors on multi-turn agent calls
signals.summary: Multi-turn agent calls with DeepSeek thinking models (deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-r1) fail on the second LLM call with 400 error because _get_request_payload() drops reasoning_content from AIMessage.additional_kwargs during serialization
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking with high frequency (4 duplicate reports): multi-turn agentic loops are completely broken for DeepSeek reasoning models. The agent fails on the second LLM call every time with a 400 error. This makes any practical use of DeepSeek thinking models (deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-r1) in agentic workflows impossible. The root cause is clear: _convert_message_to_dict() drops reasoning_content from additional_kwargs when serializing AIMessage, but DeepSeek API requires it to be passed back in subsequent requests.

First LLM call succeeds but second call fails with 400 error: 'The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.' Root cause: _get_request_payload() calls _convert_message_to_dict() which drops reasoning_content from additional_kwargs. The agent loop is completely broken for DeepSeek reasoning models.
