This blocks the core workflow of creating agents with structured output on OpenAI-compatible providers — a primary use case for LangChain agents.

signals.topic: msgpack serialization degrades Pydantic models to dict after interrupt resume when framework types are in allowed_msgpack_modules
signals.summary: Setting allowed_msgpack_modules in JsonPlusSerializer enables strict mode, causing user-defined Pydantic models to be deserialized as plain dicts. Accessing model attributes after interrupt resume raises AttributeError.
aliases: allowed_msgpack_modules strict mode breaks user models
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (#7695, #7467) share root cause: msgpack/JSON serialization layer silently fails or degrades types when handling Pydantic models or bson types. Both cause runtime AttributeError/TypeError that crashes the agent loop after interrupt resume or during MongoDB checkpointing. No opt-out workaround exists.

source_issues.title: Honor allowed_msgpack_modules in langgraph.json
source_issues.evidence: Setting allowed_msgpack_modules flips JsonPlusSerializer into strict mode. On resume, UserModel is degraded to dict and line 32 raises: AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'label'. Users of UiPath-langchain framework are affected.

source_issues.title: ObjectId handling by msgpack in MongoDb checkpointer
source_issues.evidence: When bson ObjectId is in agent state and MongoDB checkpointer uses msgpack serialization, TypeError: Object of type ObjectId is not JSON serializable is raised. No workaround exists without patching serde/jsonplus.py.

signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization causes 85% storage bloat and 38% token overhead with no opt-out path
signals.summary: MemorySaver/PostgresSaver/SqliteSaver use full Pydantic metadata serialization via dumpd() on every checkpoint write, producing 6.79x storage overhead and 37.8% token overhead in LLM context. No pluggable serializer interface exists.
signals.review_reason: Significant cost impact: 85% storage overhead and 37.8% token overhead on every checkpoint write and LLM call. Users cannot opt out of bloated serialization path. No workaround exists without forking internal classes. Financial impact quantified at ~$370K/year at scale.

source_issues.title: LangGraph checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out path - reproducible with drop-in fix
source_issues.evidence: Checkpoint storage 21,850 bytes vs 3,217 bytes with alternative serializer (85.3% overhead). Token overhead 5,764 vs 3,587 tokens (37.8%). Annual cost projection $764,200 vs $391,600 with compression. No exception raised — silent payload forwarding.

signals.topic: draw_graph TypeError sorting edges with None data from conditional edges when node returns Command[Literal[...]]
signals.summary: Calling graph.get_graph() raises TypeError when a node both returns Command[Literal[...]] and has add_conditional_edges. The sorted() calls in _draw.py cannot compare None and str in edge data fields.
signals.review_reason: Blocks graph visualization (get_graph) in specific but reproducible scenario. TypeError is a clear runtime failure. Reproducible across versions 1.1.10 through 1.2.0a5. However count=1 and affects only visualization, not core execution.

source_issues.title: draw_graph: TypeError sorting edges with None data from conditional edges
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'str'. Bug in libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_draw.py at sorted() calls. Triggered when node returns Command[Literal[...]] AND uses add_conditional_edges from same node. Affects graph.get_graph() and graph visualization.

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt/$gte/$lt/$lte) use lexicographic text comparison instead of numeric comparison
signals.summary: PostgresStore._get_filter_condition uses value->>key (text extraction) for numeric comparison operators. PostgreSQL compares strings lexicographically, so '9' >= '10' is True, silently returning wrong query results.
signals.review_reason: Silently wrong query results in PostgresStore numeric filters. Users applying range filters on numeric fields (e.g. price, score, age) get incorrect data subsets without any error or warning. SqliteStore already has the correct fix (CAST) but PostgresStore was not updated.

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: Filter {"score": {"$gte": 10}} incorrectly includes items with score=2..9 because '9' >= '10' in text ordering. SqliteStore already handles this correctly with CAST(... AS REAL) but fix was not propagated to PostgresStore.

signals.topic: PostgresSaver.setup() fails when called inside a transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY restriction
signals.summary: PostgresSaver.setup() raises ActiveSqlTransaction because MIGRATIONS contains CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY which cannot run inside a transaction block. Blocks atomic provisioning flows and implicit transaction contexts.
aliases: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside transaction failure
signals.review_reason: Prevents legitimate atomic provisioning workflows where checkpoint table setup must be transactional with other DDL operations. Affects multi-tenant deployment patterns. No clean upstream fix — users must subclass and manually strip CONCURRENTLY from migrations.

source_issues.title: PostgresSaver.setup() fails when called inside a transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
source_issues.evidence: psycopg.errors.ActiveSqlTransaction: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. Blocks atomic multi-tenant onboarding flows where tenant schema creation + checkpoint provisioning must roll back together. Workaround requires subclassing and stripping CONCURRENTLY from migrations.

signals.topic: Knowledge Retrieval node metadata filter dropdown z-index renders behind other layers, blocking operator selection
signals.summary: The metadata filter dropdown in Knowledge Retrieval nodes is not rendered at the topmost z-index layer, making operator options unclickable. Additionally, the filter always uses document_name as the key regardless of the selected operator.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot click and select metadata filter operators in the Knowledge Retrieval node because the dropdown is hidden behind other UI layers. Two independent reports confirm the same UI layer defect blocks everyday knowledge base configuration and retrieval setup. Both issues are labeled bug and involve the same Knowledge Retrieval node metadata filter component.

source_issues.title: Bug: The drop-down box for the metadata filter condition of the knowledge retrieval node is not set as layer-topmost.
source_issues.evidence: Dropdown not rendered on top layer; options are unclickable. Steps to reproduce are clearly documented with screenshots.

source_issues.title: Bug: Metadata Filter Conditions always returns document_name regardless of the operator selected
source_issues.evidence: Regardless of operator chosen, filter always uses document_name as key. Confirmed reproducible on self-hosted 1.13.3 Docker.

signals.topic: Voice input (audio-to-text) fails in published app but works in preview — key accessibility feature non-functional in production
signals.summary: Voice/audio features work correctly in app preview/debug mode but fail completely in published applications. Audio-to-text throws 'Operator getitem is not supported' error in production; TTS audio playback fails silently in browser despite valid audio response.
aliases: audio to text fails published app
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm voice/audio features work in preview/debug mode but fail in published apps. Issue #35877 prevents audio-to-text entirely in production with a type error, and #35880 shows TTS audio playback silently fails in the browser despite the audio being valid. Together they represent a complete failure of voice/audio I/O in published Dify applications, a key accessibility feature. Users cannot use voice input or hear TTS responses in their deployed apps.

source_issues.title: Voice input abnormal (audio-to-text)
source_issues.evidence: Voice input works on preview/debug page but fails after app is published with 'Operator getitem is not supported' error. Root cause identified: web API passes object instead of str to AudioService.transcript_asr.

source_issues.title: TTS audio fails to play in the browser
source_issues.evidence: TTS audio API returns correctly (verified via curl and browser fetch), audio file plays in external players, but in-browser playback fails silently. Affects published apps only.

signals.topic: Chatflow file validation fails on memory replay when allowed_file_types contains 'custom'
signals.summary: Files uploaded in round 1 of a Chatflow with memory enabled pass validation but are rejected in round 2 (replayed from conversation history) with a ValueError. Root cause: the CUSTOM file type bypass only triggers on literal 'custom' type, but replay stores the resolved type (e.g., image), losing the bypass.
aliases: custom file type bypass lost on round 2
signals.review_reason: Files uploaded in round 1 of a chatflow with memory enabled pass validation, but in round 2 (replayed from conversation history) the same files are rejected with ValueError. This breaks conversational file handling workflows entirely — users cannot continue a multi-turn conversation referencing previously uploaded files even with an unchanged workflow config. Affects Chatflow, Agent Chat, Basic Agent, and LLM nodes inside Chatflows with memory enabled.

source_issues.title: Chatflow file validation fails on memory replay when allowed_file_types is [custom]
source_issues.evidence: Round 1 file upload passes validation; Round 2 (replayed from TokenBufferMemory) fails with ValueError File validation failed. Affected: Chatflow, Agent Chat, and Basic Agent modes. Root cause precisely identified in code.

signals.topic: API document upload completes with 0 segments while GUI upload indexes correctly — silent knowledge base empty state
signals.summary: API-based document uploads return HTTP 200 with indexing_status=completed but segment_count=0 and tokens=0, making documents completely unusable for retrieval. The same documents uploaded via GUI in the same dataset with identical settings index correctly.
aliases: document indexing silent failure API path
signals.review_reason: API-based document uploads return success (200) but leave documents completely empty with 0 segments and 0 tokens, making them entirely unusable for retrieval. This causes silent data loss in programmatic ingestion pipelines — users do not realize their knowledge base is empty until they manually inspect each document. This is a critical data integrity issue for automated workflows relying on API-based document ingestion.

source_issues.title: API upload completes with 0 segments, while GUI upload indexes correctly (same dataset, self-hosted 1.13.3)
source_issues.evidence: API upload returns 200 with indexing_status=completed but segment_count=0 and tokens=0. GUI upload to the same dataset with same settings indexes correctly. Steps to reproduce with exact API calls provided.

signals.topic: Sandbox 0.2.15 Node.js code execution crashes with signal aborted — regression from 0.2.14, all Node.js code nodes broken in 1.14.0
signals.summary: Any workflow containing a Code (Node.js) node crashes with 'signal: aborted (core dumped)' in sandbox 0.2.15, while the identical code runs successfully in 0.2.14. The regression is confirmed across CentOS/RHEL environments and is triggered by DifySeccomp() during Node.js runner initialization.
signals.review_reason: All workflows containing a Code (Node.js) node crash completely with signal aborted in Dify 1.14.0 self-hosted deployments. This is a full regression — every Node.js code node in any workflow is broken for affected users. The root cause is a bug introduced in dify-sandbox 0.2.15, and the only workaround is a manual downgrade. No user can run existing Node.js code nodes without either downgrading or waiting for a fix.

source_issues.title: Sandbox 0.2.15 crashes with "signal: aborted (core dumped)" on Node.js execution — regression from 0.2.14
source_issues.evidence: Any valid Node.js code node crashes with 'signal: aborted (core dumped)' in sandbox 0.2.15. Same code works in 0.2.14. Regression confirmed across CentOS/RHEL environments. Confirmed workaround: downgrade to 0.2.14.

signals.topic: LangChain vector store search() crashes with TypeError in v2.0.0+
signals.summary: score_and_rank crashes with TypeError when LangChain vector store returns None scores, introduced in v2.0.0-beta.
signals.review_reason: Code-level crash (TypeError) in score_and_rank triggered by LangChain vector store search path. Users cannot complete search() calls with LangChain provider. Full reproduction case provided.

source_issues.title: LangChain vector store: search() crashes with TypeError in v2.0.0+
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float' in score_and_rank when dict.get() returns None instead of default. Has standalone repro script.

signals.topic: Server mode rejects multimodal messages with validation error
signals.summary: POST /memories with image_url content in server mode returns validation error, blocking multimodal use cases.
signals.review_reason: Main API endpoint (/memories) explicitly rejects multimodal payloads with a validation error in server mode (mem0 v2.0.1). Users cannot add image memories via server API — clear functional blocking of a primary workflow.

source_issues.title: I started in server mode and adding memories is not supported in multi-modal mode.
source_issues.evidence: HTTP POST to /memories with image_url payload returns FastAPI validation error: 'Input should be a valid string' at messages[0].content. Multimodal memory addition is blocked in server mode.

signals.topic: Delete API returns success without actually removing memories
signals.summary: Calling /product/delete_memory returns success response but memory persists in search results with empty delete_time field.
signals.review_reason: Delete API returns success (no error thrown) while data remains intact — a data integrity violation that silently corrupts user expectations. The memory is neither deleted nor flagged with a timestamp. This is worse than a crash because the user receives false confirmation. Active discussion with 4 comments confirms real usage impact.

source_issues.title: delete api doesn't work
source_issues.evidence: Delete API returns HTTP success but memory still appears in search results and delete_time field remains empty. Data integrity violation: API lies about deletion outcome. Has 4 comments indicating active discussion.

signals.topic: TypeScript SDK v3 silently camelizes user-defined metadata keys on read, breaking v2→v3 upgrade path
signals.summary: snakeToCamelKeys recurses into user-controlled metadata blob on every response, silently changing key casing.
signals.review_reason: TypeScript SDK silently transforms user-defined metadata keys on every read — not a crash but a silent data corruption that breaks v2→v3 upgrades without any warning. Three independent downstream failures documented: indexer invalidation, search fragmentation, and undefined adapter results.

source_issues.title: [TypeScript SDK] v3 silently camelizes user-defined `metadata` keys on read, breaking round-trip
source_issues.evidence: User stores metadata.message_id, reads back metadata.messageId. Full standalone repro without API calls. Three concrete downstream impacts documented: indexer silently classifying all new memories as invalid, keyword search fragmentation between pre/post-upgrade docs, adapters returning undefined for newly written memories.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0 agent isolation and run_id broken after OpenClaw 4.26+ upgrade
signals.summary: After OpenClaw 4.26+, register() is called multiple times per conversation causing user_id isolation failure and run_id=None.
signals.review_reason: Three inter-related functional failures in openclaw-mem0 after OpenClaw upgrade: agent isolation (critical for multi-tenant setups), session-level run_id (needed to filter memories by conversation), and autoCapture (primary memory save mechanism). Root cause identified in closure lifecycle change.

source_issues.title: [openclaw-mem0] Agent isolation & run_id broken after OpenClaw 4.26+ upgrade
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct failures after OpenClaw 4.26+ upgrade: (1) agent-level memory isolation broken — user_id not concatenated with :agent:<agent_id> suffix, (2) run_id always None breaking session filtering, (3) autoCapture broken preventing memory saves. Root cause: register() called multiple times per conversation creating separate closures.

signals.topic: Python: ChatMessageStore 导出缺失导致 1.2.x 版本 ImportError
signals.summary: agent_framework 和 agent_framework_core 的 __init__.py 均未导出 ChatMessageStore，导致用户按官方文档 import 时触发 ImportError，阻断主流程。4个独立 issue 均复现此问题，根因为重构后 ChatMessageStore 重命名为 MessageStore 但旧名称未在 __init__.py 中重新导出，且文档未同步更新。
signals.review_reason: 4个独立 issue 均来自真实用户，完整堆栈和复现步骤证明主流程阻断：用户按照官方文档 import 直接失败，且旧名称 ChatMessageStore 和新名称 MessageStore 均无法导入，明确是重构后的包导出遗漏，非单条公告或功能请求。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: can't import `ChatMessageStore` in 1.2.2
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'ChatMessageStore' from 'agent_framework' — 用户按官方文档 import 时直接失败，主流程阻断

source_issues.title: Python: Missing `ChatMessageStore` in agent_framework_core
source_issues.evidence: ChatMessageStore 在 agent_framework_core 中缺失，用户无法按文档方式导入

source_issues.title: Python: ChatMessageStore missing from agent_framework/__init__.py
source_issues.evidence: ChatMessageStore 不在 __init__.py 导出列表中，直接 import 失败

source_issues.title: Python: ChatMessageStore missing from __init__.py
source_issues.evidence: 同一包的独立报告，确认 __init__.py 导出缺失为跨版本问题

signals.topic: Python: agent_framework 元包缺少 agent_framework_core 依赖，导致 pip install agent-framework 失败或锁定在旧版本
signals.summary: 用户执行 pip install agent-framework 时元包未声明 agent_framework_core 依赖，导致安装失败。部分用户被迫锁定在 1.1.4 版本，无法升级到 1.2.x，直接影响所有新用户的环境初始化和现有用户的版本迁移。
aliases: pip install agent-framework fails due to missing dependency
signals.review_reason: 包依赖问题直接阻断环境初始化：新用户无法正常安装，已在旧版本用户无法安全升级，影响范围覆盖 Python SDK 的所有初次安装和版本迁移场景，是安装主流程的基础性失败。

source_issues.title: Python: `agent_framework` metapackage missing dependency `agent_framework_core`
source_issues.evidence: pip install agent-framework 因元包缺少 agent_framework_core 依赖而失败

source_issues.title: Python: User is stuck on version 1.1.4 because of missing dependency
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确反馈因依赖问题无法升级，被迫锁定在 1.1.4 版本

signals.topic: .NET: MultiPartyConversation._history 在工作流会话序列化后丢失，导致第二轮对话抛出 Bookmark value too large
signals.summary: MultiPartyConversation._history 为私有字段且无 [JsonInclude]，STJ 序列化 HandoffSharedState 时静默丢弃，导致反序列化后 _history 为空，下一轮对话的 CollectNewMessages 因 count<0 抛出异常。1.2 版本 MultiPartyConversation 重写后引入，独立于其他已知问题。
aliases: Bookmark value too large on turn 2
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：会话序列化是生产环境持久化的基础操作，第二轮对话必然触发 Bookmark value too large 异常崩溃。虽然仅 1 个 issue，但有完整代码证据、JsonDocument 直接验证、版本对比确认 1.0 不存在问题，属于 1.2 重写引入的明确回归。

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: MultiPartyConversation._history is dropped during workflow-as-agent session round-trip → 'Bookmark value too large' on next turn (1.3)
source_issues.evidence: Turn 2 抛出 Bookmark value too large: 2 vs count=-1，代码证据显示 _history 为 private readonly List 且无 JsonInclude，STJ 反射序列化器静默丢弃。已在 1.0.0 确认不重现，1.2 引入。提供完整可复现代码，JsonDocument 直接检查确认 conversation: {}。

signals.topic: .NET: ApprovalRequiredAIFunction 配合 externalLoop 导致 Azure Conversations API 残留 dangling function_call，第二轮批准后请求返回 HTTP 400
signals.summary: externalLoop 为 true 时，Azure Conversations API 在模型发出 function_call 时立即持久化，但 ApprovalRequiredAIFunction 在工具执行前暂停，导致 dangling function_call 无匹配 output，第二轮 POST mcp_approval_response 时返回 HTTP 400: No tool output found for function call，阻断 HITL 审批流程。
aliases: dangling function_call breaks hosted agent resume
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：HITL 审批是 Azure Foundry hosted agent 的核心功能，externalLoop+ApprovalRequiredAIFunction 是官方示例架构，第二轮批准后直接返回 HTTP 400 且无法恢复（会话在存储层已 wedged）。Workaround 要求改用不同 API 路径，改变了用户原有设计意图。

source_issues.title: .NET: `externalLoop` + `ApprovalRequiredAIFunction` leaves dangling `function_call` in Azure Conversations API, breaks resume
source_issues.evidence: 第二轮 POST mcp_approval_response 后 Azure API 返回 HTTP 400: No tool output found for function call call_J9Y...，提供完整 Repro 步骤、根因分析和 3 种可选修复方案。Workaround 存在但需要改用 workflow-level InvokeFunctionTool，不适用于 agent-level 场景。

signals.topic: .NET: 多层级工作流拓扑中 Handoffs 在第二轮及之后丢失定义的工具
signals.summary: 包含 back-edges 的多层级 handoff 工作流，第二轮开始丢失 agent 定义的工具，导致工具调用失败。与 MultiPartyConversation._history 数据丢失问题根因不同（虽然可能在同一包中），影响使用 handoff 模式的生产用户。
aliases: Handoffs lose defined tools on subsequent turns
signals.review_reason: 主流程非阻断但影响显著：第二轮工具丢失导致工作流行为异常，用户需重启会话才能继续使用完整工具集。提供 Repro 步骤，issue 来源明确。

source_issues.title: .NET: Handoffs with multi-level workflow topology lose their defined tools on subsequent turns
source_issues.evidence: Issue 5688 标题明确描述：多层级拓扑的 handoff workflow，第二轮及之后丢失定义的工具，影响 InvokeFunctionTool 和 InvokeAgent 场景。提供完整 Repro 步骤。

signals.topic: UnicodeDecodeError crash in PlaywrightController when file encoding is not UTF-8, breaking MagenticOne/WebSurfer on non-English systems
signals.summary: When running MagenticOne in non-English environments (e.g., Windows with cp950/CP936 encoding), reading page_script.js fails with UnicodeDecodeError because the open() call lacks encoding='utf-8', causing the entire MagenticOne startup to crash with a traceback in PlaywrightController.__init__.
signals.review_reason: User-reported crash that completely blocks MagenticOne startup in non-English environments. Full traceback demonstrates process termination (UnicodeDecodeError) at PlaywrightController.__init__, a core component. Not an edge case: file reading without encoding is a systemic pattern affecting any user with non-default system locale (cp936/CP950/GBK/etc.). Fix is trivial (add encoding='utf-8'), confirming the root cause.

source_issues.title: open needs encoding='utf-8' for non-english environment, error in playwright_controller.py
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp950' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 in position 11569 — full traceback from PlaywrightController.__init__ at line 68, crash occurs during MagenticOne initialization when reading page_script.js without explicit encoding, user ran m1 --rich with Chinese text and process terminated. Reporter explicitly confirmed 'simply add encoding=utf-8' fixes it.

signals.topic: Python-published messages result in 'Unhandled Message' or 'Unknown Payload' errors in distributed multi-agent runtime, causing message loss
signals.summary: When agents publish messages from Python in a distributed runtime, messages routed to the agent result in either 'Unhandled Message' or 'Unknown Payload' errors, leading to message loss and undefined agent behavior. The agent's message handler does not correctly receive or process the published messages.
aliases: message routing failure in distributed runtime
Unhandled Message error in agent pub/sub
Unknown Payload errors on publish from Python
signals.review_reason: User-documented runtime failure showing published messages are silently dropped with 'Unhandled Message' / 'Unknown Payload' errors in autogen_core, causing message loss in distributed multi-agent communication. Not blocking the entire workflow (agent continues) but represents a core functional failure where inter-agent messaging silently fails without error propagation to the user.

source_issues.title: some messages published from python are routed to the agent but result in either Unhandled Message or Unknown Payload.
source_issues.evidence: Logs show explicit 'Unhandled message: message: "from Python!"' and 'Unhandled message: UnknownPayload(type_name='', data_content_type='application/x-protobuf', payload=b'')' errors in autogen_core at runtime, indicating published messages are silently dropped rather than routed to the expected handler. User provided full repro steps via 'dotnet run' in Hello.AppHost sample. Messages successfully sent by agent but never processed by handler, causing undefined behavior.

signals.topic: Dashboard screencast freezes permanently with no error message when frame acknowledgments fail (network timeout/connection issues)
signals.summary: Dashboard video feed freezes permanently when frame acknowledgments fail due to network issues. The underlying cause is that sendMayFail() silently swallows all ack errors, leaving users with a frozen video and no indication of what went wrong.
aliases: Dashboard video feed freezes on network issues
Screencast frame ack failure causes permanent freeze
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：Dashboard screencast是Playwright可视化调试的核心功能。帧确认失败时，视频流永久冻结，用户无法继续观测测试行为，且无任何错误提示，需完全重启才能恢复。两个issue分别从不同角度报告同一问题，说明该问题在真实使用中反复出现，影响显著。

source_issues.title: Dashboard screencast freezes on frame acknowledgment failures
source_issues.evidence: Screencast protocol uses request-ack system; if ack fails browser stops sending frames. sendMayFail() silently swallows all errors. Video freezes permanently with no error shown and no recovery (requires full restart). Multiple failure scenarios: network timeout, high latency, connection interruption, session termination mid-stream.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Dashboard interactive clicks fail with remote browsers and screencast freezes
source_issues.evidence: Same screencast freeze bug reported in a separate issue alongside remote browser clicks bug. Both bugs filed together, confirming the freeze issue is a recurring problem affecting dashboard users.

signals.topic: MCP cli-client CDP browser-level commands fail in extension mode (cookie/storage/state operations broken)
signals.summary: In MCP extension mode, browser-level CDP commands (Storage.*, Browser.*) are unconditionally rejected with 'Unsupported command without sessionId' because the relay requires a sessionId that these browser-scoped commands don't carry. This breaks cookie-list, cookie-get, state-save, and all other storage/state operations in extension mode.
aliases: MCP CDP extension mode cookie commands fail
cli-client extension mode storage CDP commands broken
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：MCP extension mode是Playwright MCP的核心使用场景，用于读取用户已登录浏览器的HttpOnly cookie。当前extension mode下所有cookie/storage/state CDP命令全部失败，无法完成任何有意义的浏览器状态操作。用户已提供完整复现步骤和本地patch验证，根因已定位，阻断性明确。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: cli-client extension mode rejects all browser-level CDP commands (cookie-list, state-save) with "Unsupported command without sessionId"
source_issues.evidence: Root cause already located in cdpRelayV2.ts. Verified with full reproduction steps. Author confirms (1) cookie-list/state-save fail in extension mode but work in standalone mode, (2) HttpOnly cookies are inaccessible via eval workaround, (3) local patch confirmed to fix the issue. This blocks the core extension-mode use case: reading user's logged-in HttpOnly cookies.

signals.topic: HAR recording replay serves stale/failed response when network retried requests are recorded with duplicate entries
signals.summary: routeFromHAR in recording mode saves both the failed attempt and the successful retry as separate entries for the same URL. On replay, Playwright matches the first (failed/malformed) entry, causing tests to receive blank pages and fail.
aliases: HAR replay uses wrong entry when retried requests are recorded
routeFromHAR duplicate entries cause replay to serve failed response
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：HAR replay是Playwright测试中的核心功能。当网络瞬时错误发生时，HAR会记录重复条目，导致replay时返回错误响应，测试用例完全失败。影响覆盖所有使用HAR replay的工作流，特别是CI环境中网络不稳定场景。用户提供了完整可复现的示例仓库和明确的根因描述。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: routeFromHAR records duplicate entries for retried requests, causing replay to serve failed response
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction repo provided. When /flaky-page endpoint destroys socket on first connection (simulating transient network error), HAR saves two entries: first empty (malformed, no body), second correct. On replay, Playwright matches first entry → blank page → test fails. Real-world impact: any flaky network in CI can corrupt HAR and break all subsequent replays.

signals.topic: HAR recording truncates API request cookie values containing '=' (Base64/JWT tokens corrupted)
signals.summary: When recording HAR via page.request.* API, cookie values containing '=' (e.g. Base64 tokens, JWT cookies) are truncated at the first '='. Root cause: fetch.ts uses split('=') instead of indexOf('='), breaking on every '=' instead of only the first one.
aliases: API request cookie values with '=' truncated in HAR recording
signals.review_reason: 数据损坏：HAR recording是Playwright API测试的核心功能。含有'='的cookie值（如JWT、Base64编码token）被错误截断，导致HAR文件中的请求cookie数据损坏，直接影响所有依赖HAR replay的API测试场景。这是一个数据完整性问题，在真实环境中普遍存在（JWT/Base64 token广泛使用）。

source_issues.title: fix(har): API request cookie values containing '=' are truncated in HAR recording
source_issues.evidence: Cookie 'token=abc=xyz' recorded as 'token=abc'. Root cause pinpointed: fetch.ts uses split('=') instead of indexOf('='), splitting on every '=' rather than only the first. Real-world affected values: Base64-encoded tokens (eyJhbGc=), JWT/signed session cookies, URL-safe encoded values with padding. HAR recording is used for offline API testing and replay, making corrupted cookies a data integrity issue.

signals.topic: WebSocket connect failures on Debian12/WebKit due to localhost resolving to IPv6 (::1) while WebKit uses IPv4
signals.summary: On Debian12, localhost resolves to ::1 (IPv6) but WebKit only connects via IPv4 (127.0.0.1), causing ECONNREFUSED on all WebSocket connections. Affects 11 tests including browsertype-connect and debug-controller.
aliases: Debian12 WebKit WebSocket ECONNREFUSED localhost IPv6
WebKit Debian12 wsServer localhost resolution breaks WebSocket
signals.review_reason: CI阻断：Debian12是Playwright官方CI测试环境，该平台上有11个测试全部失败（WebSocket连接被拒绝）。wsServer默认hostname设置不当导致WebKit无法建立连接，覆盖连接和debug-controller全部核心功能。回归引入的commit已被精确定位，影响明确。

source_issues.title: [Regression]: 11 test failures on WebKit on Debian12 after a8ad57fcb4566146d4be6587c50bd7a095383ee4
source_issues.evidence: wsServer.ts defaults hostname to 'localhost' which resolves to ::1 on Debian12, but WebKit WebSocket connects to 127.0.0.1. 11 tests fail with ECONNREFUSED: browsertype-connect (wss connect), debug-controller (all 9 operations). Fix identified: change default hostname to '127.0.0.1'. Root commit pinpointed. Affects all Debian12 CI runs and local testing.

signals.topic: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync fails with NOT NULL constraint violation on json column
signals.summary: When using SqliteVectorStore's UpsertAsync method, the json column (defined as NOT NULL) receives a null or empty value from the connector's serialization, causing SQLite Error 19. Users must resort to manual raw SQL workarounds, completely bypassing the official connector.
aliases: SqliteVectorStore json column NOT NULL violation
SqliteVec connector upsert fails json column
signals.review_reason: This is a definitive user pain point: SqliteVectorStore's UpsertAsync is completely broken (NOT NULL constraint violation), forcing users to abandon the official connector and write raw SQL as a workaround. This is a primary data operation flow failure — not an edge case, but a blocker for any user trying to use SQLite as a vector store.

source_issues.title: Bug: [SqliteVectorStore] NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json during UpsertAsync
source_issues.evidence: UpsertAsync throws 'SQLite Error 19: NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json'. The json column is defined as NOT NULL but the connector serializes non-vector properties into a null/empty value. Workaround via manual raw SQL bypasses the bug entirely, confirming the connector is the root cause.

signals.topic: VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions not propagated to EmbeddingGenerationOptions, blocking automatic embedding generation with MRL models
signals.summary: Users with text embedding models that enforce a Maximum Result Length (MRL) cannot use Semantic Kernel's automatic embedding generation because VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions cannot be passed through to EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions, leaving the feature unusable for those models.
aliases: VectorStoreVectorAttribute dimensions not passed to EmbeddingGenerationOptions
automatic embedding generation fails with MRL models
signals.review_reason: This blocks automatic embedding generation for a class of widely-used embedding models (those with MRL support). Users cannot use a core convenience feature of the vector store unless they manually implement embedding generation, which defeats the purpose of the automatic flow. The user impact is clear: a primary feature is non-functional for affected models.

source_issues.title: VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions should be passed to EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions
source_issues.evidence: Users with MRL-enforcing embedding models cannot use automatic embedding generation because there is no way to specify EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions through the automatic embedding generation flow.

signals.topic: ImageContent returned from kernel functions serialized as JSON text instead of native image format in tool results
signals.summary: Kernel functions returning ImageContent have it serialized to JSON text (base64 + mimeType) rather than native image format in API tool results. This prevents Gemini 3+ and Anthropic Claude from 'seeing' the image, as they receive text instead of an actual image — breaking multimodal tool calling for these connectors.
aliases: ImageContent serialized as JSON instead of native image format
ImageContent tool results not using native format for Gemini/Anthropic
ImageContent not passed natively to multimodal connectors
signals.review_reason: This breaks multimodal tool calling for Gemini 3+ and Anthropic connectors — two of the most capable multimodal models. The feature technically 'works' (no crash) but produces wrong output (text instead of image), defeating the purpose of returning ImageContent. Users relying on vision capabilities in agent tool use will see degraded or incorrect model responses.

source_issues.title: Bug: ImageContent in tool/function results is serialized to JSON instead of native format
source_issues.evidence: When a kernel function returns ImageContent, the connector serializes it to JSON text. The API receives '{Data: base64..., MimeType: image/png}' as text rather than an actual image. Gemini 3+ and Anthropic Claude natively support images in tool results (inlineData / ImageBlockParam), but the current serialization prevents them from processing images correctly.

signals.topic: Computer Use and Browser Use skills unavailable or broken across Desktop App, Settings panel, and Windows WSL environments
signals.summary: Three issues converge on Browser Use / Computer Use unavailability: (1) Computer Use does not appear in Codex Settings despite the bundled plugin and helper app being installed. (2) On Windows 11 WSL2, Browser Use fails because the required mcp__node_repl__js tool is not exposed and the browser-use backend socket is missing. (3) Browser Use IAB rethrows CDP command timeouts as generic failures instead of classifying recoverable commands and retrying.
signals.review_reason: Browser Use and Computer Use are key Codex skills that are unavailable or unreliable across multiple environments. Issue #21579 shows a plugin discovery/loading bug making Computer Use completely absent from Settings. Issue #21575 blocks Browser Use entirely on Windows WSL, a common developer environment. Issue #21560 shows IAB lacks retry logic for recoverable CDP timeouts, causing safe operations to fail sessions unnecessarily.

source_issues.title: Computer Use does not appear in Settings despite plugin and helper existing
source_issues.evidence: Plugin exists with enabled=true in config.toml, bundled plugin path exists, plugin cache entry exists, helper app exists, but Computer Use actions are unavailable and feature does not appear in Settings UI; no workaround

source_issues.title: Browser Use not available on Windows 11 WSL: no node_repl tool or browser-use socket

source_issues.title: Browser Use IAB should classify recoverable CDP command timeouts instead of cleanup-and-rethrow
source_issues.evidence: Page.captureScreenshot timed out at ~20s and IAB rethrew as generic failure; title/URL/console inspection worked before and after; recovery test in fresh session succeeded for same URL; safe idempotent commands should be retried, not treated as fatal

signals.topic: Codex Desktop sidebar hides older chats and closed side chats are lost despite data existing on disk
signals.summary: Two related session state bugs: (1) The sidebar hides older local project chats even though thread data exists in state_5.sqlite, session_index.jsonl, and rollout files on disk — selective indexing/hydration failure. (2) Side chat queued/steer messages route to the main chat instead of staying in the side chat, and closed side chats cannot be recovered through any UI path. Both cause loss of user work context despite data persistence at the storage layer.
aliases: session data exists but not visible
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but related session state failures both result in user work context being lost or inaccessible despite data existing on disk. Issue #21581 shows data exists at the storage layer but the UI fails to display it (indexing/hydration bug). Issue #21583 shows side chat isolation is broken and closed chats are permanently unrecoverable. Together they represent a pattern of session state management failure causing direct loss of user work.

source_issues.title: Desktop sidebar/search hides older local project chats although thread data still exists on disk
source_issues.evidence: Verified data exists in state_5.sqlite (threads rows with archived=0, source=vscode), session_index.jsonl (IDs present), rollout-*.jsonl (files exist); only workaround is cloning to a new thread ID with new rollout file path

source_issues.title: Side chat queued/steer messages route to main chat, and closed side chats are lost
source_issues.evidence: Messages queued or steered in a side chat are incorrectly added to the main conversation; closed side chats are not recoverable from parent chat, history, or any UI path; effectively loses session context and user work

signals.topic: Desktop App serializes shell/apply_patch command array as JSON string, breaking both tools on Windows
signals.summary: The Desktop App (version 26.429.61741) serializes the command array as a JSON string instead of a native array, causing shell and apply_patch tool calls to fail with parse errors. The identical relay setup with CLI 0.128.0 works fine, confirming the bug is in the Desktop App client with no workaround.
aliases: Windows desktop app tool call serialization
signals.review_reason: Two core tool call mechanisms (shell + apply_patch) are completely broken for Desktop App Windows users. The root cause is confirmed as incorrect JSON serialization in the Desktop App client, with no workaround. This blocks automated scripting and patch application workflows for affected users.

source_issues.title: Bug: shell/apply_patch broken in Desktop App 26.429.61741 — command array serialized as string
source_issues.evidence: shell fails with 'failed to parse function arguments: invalid type: string, expected a sequence'; apply_patch fails with 'unsupported call'; root cause confirmed as Desktop App client serialization bug; identical CLI+relay setup works; no workaround available

signals.topic: Codex macOS app launches but never creates UI window on Apple Silicon — process hangs in running-active-NotVisible state
signals.summary: On Apple Silicon Macs, the Codex macOS app launches and appears active in the Dock but never creates a UI window. The process enters a running-active-NotVisible state. Multiple troubleshooting attempts (reinstall, clean profile, Electron flags, cache removal) all fail. The app hangs before its own logging initializes, making self-diagnosis impossible. This completely blocks the main workflow as users cannot sign in or open any project.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow-blocking bug: users pay for Codex but cannot use it at all on Apple Silicon hardware because no window is ever created. The hang occurs before any user-facing functionality is accessible and no workaround exists. Despite count=1, the impact is total app unavailability for an entire hardware platform (Apple Silicon), qualifying it as P0 with explicit strong evidence.

source_issues.title: Codex macOS app launches but never creates a window; process remains running-active-NotVisible
source_issues.evidence: Consistently reproducible on Apple Silicon Macs; Dock icon bounces indefinitely with no window; AppleScript confirms no windows exist; Electron startup flags do not help; bundled CLI also hangs when invoked directly; regression linked to issue #11303

signals.topic: gpt-5.5 compact_remote context compaction fails reliably on Azure OpenAI / Foundry, blocking long-session workflows
signals.summary: When Codex CLI runs against Azure OpenAI / Azure Foundry endpoints and context approaches ~244k tokens, the compact_remote path calls a ChatGPT-authenticated-only endpoint, resulting in 'high demand' errors. This reliably stalls all sessions on Azure deployments. An A/B test confirms the issue is gpt-5.5-specific and reproduces across distinct Azure deployment variants.
signals.review_reason: All Codex CLI sessions against Azure OpenAI / Foundry are blocked when context grows large, which is a natural occurrence in production coding workflows. The compact_remote path routes to a ChatGPT-authenticated endpoint instead of Azure, meaning long sessions are structurally unreliable for Azure users. This directly blocks professional usage of Codex with Azure deployments.

source_issues.title: gpt-5.5 compact_remote: high demand reliably fails on Azure OpenAI / Foundry
source_issues.evidence: A/B test across two distinct Azure deployment variants confirms gpt-5.5-specific issue; compact_remote calls ChatGPT-authenticated endpoint even when Codex runs against Azure Foundry; reliably reproduces at ~244k token context threshold; stalls all long sessions on Azure

signals.topic: OpenAIConversationsSession silently loses assistant message history on GPT-5.4/5.5
signals.summary: OpenAIConversationsSession silently drops prior assistant messages on gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.5, producing [u, u, u, u, a] shape instead of [u, a, u, a, u, a, u, a], breaking the documented Sessions contract of persistent conversation context. Works correctly on gpt-4.1 and gpt-5.2.
aliases: silent item unlinking on newer models
signals.review_reason: Confirmed silent data loss in core session functionality affecting multiple model versions. User provided complete repro with concrete output demonstrating history corruption. This breaks the documented Sessions contract and is a primary use case for the SDK.

source_issues.title: OpenAIConversationsSession loses prior assistant items
source_issues.evidence: User provided full repro script. After N turns of [user→assistant], only the most recent assistant message survives. Conversation ends up shaped [u,u,u,u,a] instead of [u,a,u,a,u,a,u,a]. Verified against gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.5. gpt-4.1 and gpt-5.2 work correctly. SDK items are confirmed persisted server-side but unlinked from conversation by the API.

signals.topic: WebSocket transport returns HTTP 401, blocking all requests

While labeled 'server issue', from the SDK user's perspective this is a blocking failure of the agent run workflow with no workaround described. High user impact even if root cause may be server-side.

signals.topic: Local skills incompatibility with Azure OpenAI causes BadRequestError
signals.summary: Local skills work correctly with official OpenAI API but fail with Azure OpenAI due to a JSON unmarshalling error (400 BadRequestError: 'json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field ToolDefinitionForResponses.tools.environment of type string'), making local skills entirely unusable with Azure deployments.
signals.review_reason: Core feature (local skills) is completely blocked when using Azure OpenAI. User provided complete repro with exact error message showing a schema mismatch. This is a platform-specific integration regression that prevents an entire feature category from working with Azure deployments.

source_issues.title: Cannot use local skills while using GPT model APIs provided by Azure
source_issues.evidence: User provided full repro code. Same Agent setup works with official OpenAI model but throws BadRequestError with Azure client. Error: 'json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field ToolDefinitionForResponses.tools.environment of type string'. Azure works fine without local skills.

signals.topic: Session compaction can permanently delete session history on write failure
signals.summary: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession.run_compaction() clears the underlying session before writing compacted replacement items. If the write (add_items) fails after the clear succeeds, the original session history is permanently lost with no recovery path. Affects all persistent session backends (SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, Dapr, etc.).
aliases: session compaction history loss on failure
signals.review_reason: Permanent and irreversible data loss in session compaction — a core SDK feature for managing token budgets. The clear-then-add pattern creates a window where failure leaves session history permanently deleted. This is a data durability issue with clear user impact in production environments using compaction.

source_issues.title: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession can lose session history if add_items fails after clear
source_issues.evidence: Author provided full repro with mock session demonstrating: clear_session() succeeds, add_items() raises RuntimeError, resulting in empty session history. Original history gone with no recovery. Affects any persistent backend that can fail between clear and add.

signals.topic: MCP invalid JSON errors leak raw tool input despite DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA setting
signals.summary: MCP invalid JSON errors include raw tool input in the exception string even when DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA is enabled, causing sensitive data (tokens, cookies, internal URLs, user data) to leak through exception strings that commonly appear in application logs, traces, and alerting systems.
aliases: MCP data leak in error messages
sensitive data in MCP exception strings
signals.review_reason: Explicit data-security misconfiguration bypass — the DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA setting is specifically designed to prevent sensitive data exposure, yet exception strings bypass this protection. This is a confirmed security misconfiguration with evidence of real data types being leaked (tokens, cookies, URLs).

source_issues.title: MCP invalid JSON errors still include raw tool input when DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Author provided repro demonstrating that DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA suppresses debug logs but the raised ModelBehaviorError still contains the raw malformed input: 'Invalid JSON input for tool test_tool: {"secret":"SECRET_TOKEN_123"'. MCP inputs commonly carry tokens, cookies, and user data.

signals.topic: Streaming accumulate_delta drops tool_call fragments with duplicate index values in first chunk
signals.summary: The streaming accumulate_delta function in _deltas.py has a bug where multiple tool_call entries with the same index in the first chunk are stored as separate list elements instead of being merged. This causes tool_call arguments to become unparseable JSON (e.g. '{"city"' + ': "London"}' ending up split across orphaned list entries). The bug also exists in _assistants.py and the initial snapshot seeding in _completions.py.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed SDK bug with two independent user reports. When streaming tool_calls with speculative decoding (e.g. vLLM), duplicate-index entries in the first chunk are not merged, causing tool_call arguments to become unparseable JSON. This blocks the core tool-use agent workflow. Count=2 meets the threshold for a significant user-impacting issue, but is not P0 because it is a specific edge case in streaming rather than a universal API failure.

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk are accumulated incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: First chunk with two tool_calls entries at index=0 causes arguments to be split across orphaned list entries, producing invalid JSON. Observed with vLLM speculative decoding.

source_issues.title: `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when one chunk has multiple entries at the same `index`
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows accumulate_delta storing '{"city"' in acc['tool_calls'][1] while acc['tool_calls'][0] only gets ': "London"}'. JSON parsing fails. Root cause: early-return branches in _deltas.py skip index-merge logic.

signals.topic: Responses stream accumulator crashes with AttributeError when output_item.added has item=None
signals.summary: The Responses stream accumulator in openai/lib/streaming/responses/_responses.py does not guard against a null item in response.output_item.added events. When a custom OpenAI-compatible provider sends item: null, the SDK crashes with 'AttributeError: NoneType object has no attribute type', which cannot be caught or recovered from by application code.
signals.review_reason: This is a hard crash that blocks the Responses streaming workflow entirely when using OpenAI-compatible custom providers. The SDK unconditionally dereferences event.item.type without checking for None, causing an uncaught AttributeError that cannot be handled by application code. Count=1 means it cannot be P0 under the rules, but the crash severity (unrecoverable, in production) warrants P1.

source_issues.title: Responses stream accumulator crashes when response.output_item.added has item=None
source_issues.evidence: Crash occurs with AttributeError inside the SDK stream accumulator before application-level code can recover. User hit this in production against a custom provider. A defensive guard (checking item is not None before accessing .type) would prevent the crash.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely with file status stuck at in_progress
signals.summary: The upload_and_poll() method for vector store files can hang forever. The file uploads and attaches successfully, but the vector store file processing/indexing step leaves the file stuck at status='in_progress' indefinitely with no error, causing upload_and_poll() to never return. The raw file shows status='processed', but the vector_store_file stays in_progress with last_error=null.
signals.review_reason: upload_and_poll() hanging indefinitely is a workflow blocker. When vector store file processing gets stuck (file stays in_progress forever), the method blocks forever with no timeout or error signal, preventing any dependent workflow from completing. This is a clear user-facing production impact.

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows upload_and_poll() hanging indefinitely. Explicit polling confirms vector_store_file.status=='in_progress' forever while raw_file.status=='processed'. upload_and_poll() never returns, blocking any dependent workflow.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError in multiprocess forkserver workers with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12
signals.summary: Using openai SDK with pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers causes intermittent PydanticUserError ('Pydantic models should inherit from BaseModel, BaseModel cannot be instantiated directly'). With DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true (default), ~0.6% error rate with millions of requests; with false, ~9.5% error rate causing all requests to fail for affected workers. The hardcoded _parent_namespace_depth=5 in pydantic's model_rebuild causes silent failures in forkserver context.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed production issue in high-scale deployments (700 workers, millions of requests). The PydanticUserError causes request failures, with up to 9.5% failure rate when DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false. The issue directly affects the main request-handling flow and is reproducible in a production forkserver environment.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: In a forkserver setup with ~700 workers processing millions of requests: DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true gives ~0.6% error rate growing over time; DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false gives ~9.5% error rate causing ALL requests for affected workers to fail. Clear production impact at scale.

signals.topic: Async Responses .parse() causes unbounded memory growth from Pydantic schema rebuilds
signals.summary: Using AsyncResponses .parse() with Pydantic models causes unbounded memory growth. The parsing code uses TypeVar-subscripted generics (e.g. ParsedResponse[TextFormatT]) with construct_type_unchecked, but Pydantic cannot resolve the free TypeVar so model_rebuild always fails. This causes a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) to be allocated on every .parse() call, accumulating without bound until OOM.
aliases: unbounded pydantic schema rebuild memory leak
signals.review_reason: Memory leak confirmed with flame graph evidence. Each .parse() call allocates heavy Pydantic SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer objects that are never freed because the TypeVar cannot be resolved. Long-running servers making repeated structured output calls will grow memory without bound until OOM. This is a clear production reliability issue.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph confirms memory leak. Root cause: Pydantic's MockCoreSchema._built_memo is never populated because model_rebuild fails on unresolved TypeVar. Each .parse() call allocates new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) that accumulate without bound. Long-running server will OOM.

aliases: Claude ACP runtime controls fail with Internal error
ACP_TURN_FAILED on /acp spawn claude with runtime options

source_issues.title: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED while direct acpx claude succeeds
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED / Internal error while direct acpx claude succeeds. Automatic Codex + Claude two-agent ACP flow is blocked. Temporary workaround requires Codex standard ACP + Claude CLI/manual review.

source_issues.title: Claude ACP config option handling: generic runtime controls fail while clean/model-only path works

signals.topic: openclaw update leaves gateway in half-updated state — wrong install root targeted, systemd service not restarted
signals.summary: The openclaw update mechanism fails in two related ways on multi-install hosts: (1) When npm config prefix is stale, the updater targets /usr/lib/node_modules instead of the user's actual install root, producing EACCES failures and preventing the documented upgrade path. (2) After a successful disk update, the restart step only detects user-level systemd services but not system-level openclaw.service, leaving the running gateway process on the old version while the package on disk is newer. This produces a half-state with module-not-found errors in diagnostics.
aliases: update restart step does not detect systemd service scope
openclaw update targets wrong install root stale npm prefix
systemd service not restarted after openclaw update
signals.review_reason: The update mechanism has two distinct but related failures: wrong install root targeted (blocks upgrade path with misleading EACCES) and service not restarted (leaves gateway in half-updated state). Combined, these cause operators to believe an upgrade succeeded when the running process is still old, leading to confusing version skew diagnostics and potential module-not-found runtime errors. Medium-high severity: not a full block but causes operational confusion and upgrade failures.

source_issues.title: openclaw update restart step should detect systemd service scope

Fresh 5.6 CLI talking to old 5.5 process produced 'Cannot find module task-registry.maintenance-*.js'. High severity: apparent success with real operational drift.

source_issues.title: openclaw update should prefer calling-binary install root over stale npm prefix

The documented upgrade path is blocked for any user with misconfigured npm prefix. Requires NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX override to proceed.

signals.topic: Uncaught exceptions (OSError/QueryError/ImportError/ValueError) crash the application at various entry points
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught exceptions in four distinct scenarios: (1) OSError 'File name too long' in pathlib.py when --extra-system-prompt is extremely long on Linux; (2) tree_sitter QueryError in repomap.py when parsing certain Python files with invalid node type 'module'; (3) greenlet DLL load failure on Windows causing ImportError in web scraper; (4) ValueError in exceptions.py when litellm returns a PermissionDeniedError not in aider's known exceptions list. All four represent missing error handling that completely blocks the main flow.
aliases: greenlet DLL ImportError crash on Windows
unhandled exceptions crash aider during startup and normal use
signals.review_reason: Four distinct uncaught exceptions that all cause the application to crash and block the main workflow. These are all caught exception types that should be handled gracefully by aider's code. (1) OSError from extreme prompt lengths is an unhandled edge case during startup. (2) tree_sitter QueryError crashes repo-map generation which is core to aider's operation. (3) greenlet DLL failure on Windows blocks the /web command entirely for Windows users. (4) litellm's PermissionDeniedError is an unhandled new exception type that blocks all LLM communication. All four represent clear missing error handling causing application crashes — textbook P0 main-flow blocking issues.

signals.topic: LLM edit-block emits doubled path prefixes causing files to be written to wrong locations
signals.summary: When using small/less-common editor models (groq/llama-3.3-70b, openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b, gemini-2.5-flash-lite), the LLM occasionally emits edit-block headers with the chat file's own directory prefix duplicated (e.g. .claude/.claude/foo.json instead of .claude/foo.json). The existing prepended-dir guard only handles single-segment cases, so multi-segment doubled prefixes fall through silently. Files land at the doubled path and the canonical path becomes a 0-byte stub. Data corruption of edited files occurs.

doubled directory paths from LLM edit output

signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: small models trigger a specific code path in aider's wholefile/editblock coders that produces incorrect file paths. The result is silent data corruption — edited files are written to wrong locations and canonical paths become 0-byte stubs. The issue has been observed repeatedly in production (≥6 dispatches). While count=1, the root cause is clearly in aider's code, not the model, and the impact (data loss/corruption of user files) is severe. Downgraded to P1 from P0 only because count=1.

source_issues.title: Edit-block path doubling: small models hallucinate prefix-doubled headers; existing prepended-dir guard misses multi-segment cases

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/google streaming parser drops complete no-args function calls, losing thoughtSignature and breaking Gemini 3 multi-turn

The thoughtSignature attached to that chunk is also lost. The resulting 'missing thought_signature' 400 blocks the agent's next step. Has reproduction code and a clear fix.

source_issues.title: `@ai-sdk/google` streaming parser drops no-args function calls, losing `thoughtSignature`

signals.topic: Turbopack dynamic import() failures are permanently cached with no retry mechanism

signals.summary: The turbo daemon remains alive after command completion and consumes 100% CPU indefinitely. Issue reproduced with custom remote cache and turbo gen plop config, but not in clean `create-turbo` repo, indicating a specific repo configuration triggers it.
aliases: turbo daemon cpu 100 percent after completion
signals.review_reason: P1: Two related but distinct resource issues: (1) daemon 100% CPU idle consuming hardware resources indefinitely, (2) cache growing unbounded causing CI time to balloon. Both are persistent resource/cost problems rather than workflow blockers. count=2, both with multiple community comments, high confidence. P1 because while impactful, the core turbo run/build workflow continues to function.

source_issues.title: Turbo daemon uses 100% CPU even when no tasks are running
source_issues.evidence: After running a turborepo command, the turbo process stays alive consuming 100% CPU even after command completion. Video evidence attached. Repro with `pnpm turbo daemon start`. Does not reproduce in clean `create-turbo` repo, only in repo with custom remote cache (TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY) and turbo gen plop config. 29 comments indicating this affects multiple users.

source_issues.title: Cache keeps growing indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: Cache grows unbounded in CI — hundreds of MBs in days/weeks. Saving/restoring cache in CI becomes increasingly time-consuming. No automatic cleanup or `--refresh-cache` flag to control growth. 20 comments with multiple users experiencing the same cache bloat issue.

signals.topic: turbo prune generates invalid Bun lockfile causing Docker builds to fail
signals.summary: When running `turbo prune --docker`, the generated `bun.lock` file contains nested npm package entries that reference other entries dropped during pruning, causing `bun install --frozen-lockfile` to fail in Docker builds.
signals.review_reason: P0: Blocks the Docker CI/CD workflow entirely — `turbo prune --docker` is a core use case for generating lean Docker images. The pruned bun.lock becomes invalid for frozen install, causing the entire Docker build to fail. Clear reproduction with public repo and exact error messages. count=1 is acceptable here as the issue is highly specific (Bun + nested npm packages + prune interaction) and the user impact is a complete workflow failure.

source_issues.title: Turbo prune emits invalid Bun lockfile for pruned workspace with nested npm package entries
source_issues.evidence: Docker build fails at `RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` with error: `Failed to resolve prod dependency '@npmcli/metavuln-calculator' for package 'npm/@npmcli/arborist'`. Root cause: pruned lockfile keeps a package whose nested dependency target was dropped during prune. Full reproduction steps provided with a public repro repo.

signals.topic: Turbo silently scans entire home directory when project .git is absent, causing indefinite hang
signals.summary: When a project is downloaded as a ZIP (no .git folder), turbo walks up the filesystem and finds the user's home directory .git, then scans all ~500k+ files under it causing a silent indefinite hang with zero output.
aliases: turbo hangs when no .git in project
signals.review_reason: P0: Completely blocks the primary workflow (`turbo run`) for any developer who cloned via ZIP or has an unrelated `.git` in a parent directory. The failure mode is a silent hang — no error, no warning, just minutes/hours of zero-output blocking. User must kill the process to recover. This is a catastrophic experience degradation with clear root cause.

source_issues.title: Turbo silently scans entire home directory and hangs when project has no .git (ZIP download)
source_issues.evidence: User downloads project as ZIP from Gitea — no .git present. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to home dir `.git`. Turbo scans all ~500k files under home directory (`.bun/cache`, `.fnm`, `Library/Application Support`, etc.) with no error/warning, just silent hang. `--verbosity=3` confirms this. Completely blocks any turbo command from running for this common developer workflow.

signals.topic: Turbo 2.9.7 regression spawns duplicate high-CPU child turbo processes for persistent tasks under tmux
signals.summary: Upgrading to turbo 2.9.7 causes extra `turbo run dev` child processes to spawn for each persistent task, each consuming ~90-100% CPU. Issue only occurs under tmux and was fixed by downgrading to 2.9.6, indicating a regression.
aliases: turbo 2.9.7 persistent task high cpu tmux
extra turbo child processes high cpu 2.9.7
signals.review_reason: P1: This is a confirmed regression (2.9.7 vs 2.9.6) that causes high CPU usage (full core per extra process). While the underlying tasks still complete, the machine resource impact is significant — especially in environments where developers run persistent dev servers. The clear before/after with downgrade confirmation gives high confidence this is a real bug, but count=1 limits it from P0.

source_issues.title: Turbo 2.9.7 spawns high-CPU child turbo processes for persistent tasks under tmux
source_issues.evidence: Upgraded from 2.9.6 to 2.9.7. With 8 persistent tasks, 8 extra `turbo run dev` child processes appear, each at ~90-100% CPU. Dev servers still work but machine becomes very hot/noisy. Downgrading to 2.9.6 immediately fixes it. Reproduced with both default UI and --ui=stream. Control test confirms 2.9.6 behavior is correct.

signals.topic: vercel env add --value silently stores empty string — production secrets/keys fail silently
signals.summary: The CLI command `vercel env add` with `--value` flag silently stores an empty string instead of the actual value, while reporting success. Affects both plain `--value` writes (CLI 53.x) and `--sensitive` writes (since 50.5.0). This breaks production apps: HMAC verification fails, API keys are missing, and operators only discover the issue when application code reads empty `process.env` values in production.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is broken: vercel env add reports success but silently stores empty values for environment variables. This directly blocks CI/CD scripting (vercel env add ... --value ... --yes is the documented non-interactive flow) and causes production failures that are hard to debug — operators only notice when their application reads an empty process.env key (e.g. broken HMAC verification, missing signing keys). The regression spans two distinct failure modes (plain --value since 53.x, --sensitive since 50.5.0) with no error output hiding the failure from operators.

source_issues.title: vercel env add: --value silently stored as empty string (CLI 53.x), and --sensitive empty since 50.5.0
source_issues.evidence: CLI reports 'Added Environment Variable' success but stores empty value; verified with vercel env pull returning NAME=''; affects all scripting flows using --value; silent failure means operators discover only in production when process.env.NAME is empty (broken HMAC, missing API keys)

signals.topic: vercel build produces unexpected TypeScript errors that local tsc does not report
signals.summary: Running `vercel build` generates TypeScript errors (TS2339 on Response.body, drizzle-orm type mismatches) that do not occur when running tsc/tsup locally. The build succeeds through the package.json build command (tsup) but then Vercel's own build layer adds additional type checking that surfaces errors, blocking the deployment.
aliases: build-time type checking discrepancy with local tsc
signals.review_reason: Main deployment flow is blocked: users cannot deploy their projects via vercel build because the platform's build layer emits TypeScript errors that do not exist when developers run tsc/tsup locally. This is a significant workflow disruption — developers must add 'as any' workarounds (type-unsafe code) to unblock deployments, directly reducing development velocity and code quality.

source_issues.title: vercel build TS errors (hono/turborepo/drizzle)
source_issues.evidence: vercel build fails with TS2339: Property 'body' does not exist on type 'Response' and drizzle-orm type mismatches; reproducible on forked repo rt-stack connected to Vercel; same code compiles with tsc/tsup locally; default vercel build command (turbo run build --filter=...) surfaces errors that tsc does not

signals.topic: Prerender Functions do not forward URL query parameters to underlying functions (Output API v3)
signals.summary: Using Output API v3, Prerender Functions do not forward URL query parameters to the underlying function handler — request.query is always empty ({}). The documented `passQuery: true` option causes the function to always fail with a 500 error with no log output.
aliases: prerender functions cannot access query string
signals.review_reason: Key functionality is unavailable in Prerender Functions (Output API v3): users relying on query parameter handling for ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) use cases cannot access request.query at all. The documented fix (passQuery: true) worsens the situation by causing 500 errors with no observability. This blocks a core platform primitive for a real-world use case (accessing query params in ISR routes).

source_issues.title: Unable to read URL query parameters in Prerender Functions
source_issues.evidence: request.query is always {} in Prerender Functions with Output API v3; same query params work correctly in simple Serverless non-Prerender Functions; documented passQuery option causes function to fail with 500 error and no log output; this blocks ISR/incremental static regeneration use cases that rely on query parameter handling

signals.topic: Vercel Security Checkpoint false positive blocks legitimate users with no recourse to report
signals.summary: Legitimate users are blocked by the Vercel Security Checkpoint (Code 11) when visiting valid third-party websites. Users encounter a 'Failed to verify your browser Code 11' error with no way to report the false positive and no contact channel to resolve the block.
aliases: security checkpoint false positive blocking users
signals.review_reason: Experience degradation with no resolution path: legitimate users are blocked by a false-positive security checkpoint with no mechanism to report the issue or get unblocked. While the impact is to the visitor rather than the Vercel customer directly, it damages Vercel's reputation and the customer's ability to serve their users — blocking access to the customer's deployed content with zero recourse.

source_issues.title: False positive 'Failed to verify your browser Code 11 Vercel Security Checkpoint'
source_issues.evidence: User blocked by Security Checkpoint Code 11 when visiting a legitimate third-party site (docs.arbitrum.io); error provides no link or mechanism to report false positive; no accessible contact channel to resolve block; user is completely stuck

signals.topic: Remote session state not preserved after SSH reconnection (project panel, agent messages, file links)
signals.summary: After an SSH reconnection, multiple session states are lost: the project panel directory tree collapses, unsubmitted agent panel messages are lost, and file links in agent responses continue to show macOS -50 errors.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct session state components (project panel, agent messages, file links) all fail to persist across SSH reconnections — a critical workflow disruptor for remote development. Users lose unsaved work (agent messages), navigation context (project tree), and file navigation (agent links) every time a connection drops.

source_issues.title: Message text in agent panel lost with SSH disconnect
source_issues.evidence: User types an unsubmitted message in the Claude Code agent panel, loses SSH connection, reconnects — message panel is empty. User work is silently discarded.

source_issues.title: Project panel state not preserved after SSH reconnection
source_issues.evidence: User expands project panel directory tree several levels deep, loses SSH connection, reconnects — tree is fully collapsed. Navigation context is completely lost.

source_issues.title: Agent file links still show macOS -50 dialog in remote sessions after #53229
source_issues.evidence: Despite a previous fix attempt (#53229), file links in agent responses still trigger '-50' macOS errors in remote sessions, preventing users from navigating to files referenced by the agent.

signals.topic: Opening a new file silently closes previously open files, causing unsaved data loss
signals.summary: When opening a new file in Zed, previously open files are closed without warning, even if they have unsaved changes. This results in silent data loss.
aliases: unsaved changes lost on file open
signals.review_reason: Direct data loss bug with reproducible video evidence. Zed closes previously open files without any warning or prompt, even when those files contain unsaved changes. This is a primary workflow disruption — users lose work silently during normal file navigation.

source_issues.title: zed 1.1.6 closes open files with no warning, even when file has changes, losing changes
source_issues.evidence: User provides video attachment showing opening file2 replaces file1, opening file3 replaces file2, and opening file1 after editing file4 loses all changes to file4. Clear data loss with reproduction steps on macOS 15.7.5.

signals.topic: ACP cron jobs created via CronCreate never fire in Claude Code agent sessions
signals.summary: Cron jobs scheduled via the Claude Code agent's CronCreate tool never fire, even when confirmed active in CronList. The recurring task automation core feature is non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Core agent automation feature is completely non-functional. The cron scheduling system confirms the job is active but never fires — the agent's recurring task capability is broken at a fundamental level. This blocks the primary use case for loop/scheduled agent workflows.

source_issues.title: ACP cron tool created via CronCreate never fires (Claude Code agent)
source_issues.evidence: User asks agent to schedule a recurring cron with /loop 1m, CronCreate is called with correct cron expression, CronList confirms job is scheduled, user waits 2+ minutes and zero firings occur. The core recurring automation feature of the agent is entirely non-functional.

signals.topic: FS polling watcher causes excessive CPU usage (300-500%) on remote NFS workspaces
signals.summary: File system polling on remote workspaces (especially with broken symlinks on NFS mounts) causes the zed-remote-server process to spike to 300-500% CPU, making the editor unusable.
signals.review_reason: Severe performance degradation that renders the editor unusable on remote NFS workspaces — a common development setup. CPU usage at 300-500% on a single process is a resource exhaustion condition that blocks development work entirely on affected projects.

source_issues.title: FS polling watcher excessive cpu usage on remote workspace
source_issues.evidence: User reports zed-remote-server jumps to 300-500% CPU usage when a broken symlink exists in the project on NFS mount. Log spam shows repeated IO errors for every polling cycle. The editor becomes practically unusable on affected network filesystem setups.

signals.topic: ESLint LSP fails to initialize when npm ignore-scripts=true is set in .npmrc
signals.summary: ESLint language server fails to start in Zed when ignore-scripts=true is configured in ~/.npmrc, blocking linting for affected projects.
signals.review_reason: A valid and common npm security configuration (ignore-scripts=true) completely breaks ESLint LSP initialization, blocking the core linting workflow. This is not a fringe case — ignoring npm scripts is a recommended security practice. Key development tool is non-functional for affected users.

source_issues.title: ESLint LSP fails to initialize in Zed with ignore-scripts=true
source_issues.evidence: Setting ignore-scripts=true in ~/.npmrc causes ESLint LSP to fail initialization. Linting is a critical development workflow for many teams, and this configuration (a valid npm security practice) completely breaks Zed's linting support.
